Maruna/Relationships

Nastikas
Gandharva

He and Maruna have a sort of surrogate father-son relationship. Gandharva has been Maruna's teacher and protector for around 300 years. Maruna once believed that the training he was forced to undergo was harsh, but he quickly changed his mind later, when he experienced worse. Although Gandharva would always appear jealous when Shakuntala showed attention to Maruna, a bond obviously grew between the two.[2][3]

Maruna originally did not understand Gandharva's way of ruling because it was very different from his father's, but he grew to acknowledge Gandharva's attempts to maintain peace.

Within the story, Maruna appears to be the only one Gandharva can lean on, and Gandharva repeatedly takes action to protect Maruna, or grant Maruna's requests, even at personal cost.[6][7] Similarly, Maruna steps in when Gandharva is being threatened, and he worries about his mentor, and cares about his wishes even when furthering his own goals.[8]

Gandharva will often light-heartedly tease Maruna, clearly seeing through Maruna's attempts to appear serious.[9][10] When Gandharva was disappointed with Maruna, he refused to speak to Maruna and tried to leave him out of further plans for his own safety.[11]

In season 3, Gandharva largely loses Maruna's respect, because he increasingly pushes for protecting people and attempts to adopt their habits and live with them, which Maruna cannot understand and interprets as a loss of pride.[12][13][14] Regardless, he remains considerate of Gandharva's wishes and worries about his safety in threatening situations.[15][16]

In season 2, Gandharva gifted a pair of red gloves to Maruna.[17] Although Maruna complained that he does not appreciate items made by humans, he has been wearing the gloves since, only taking them off for combat so as not to damage them.[18] After the two of them have a disagreement in season 3, Maruna stops wearing the gloves.[19]

Sagara

Food! Maruna claims not to trust Sagara and threatens to eat her on several occasions, yet he lets her manipulate him and ends up doing her bidding numerous times. Sagara also seems cautious around Maruna, because she acknowledges his ability to make good on his threats to eat her and she is aware that Maruna has eaten many of his clanmates, yet she is mostly certain of her ability to reach her goals with him.

Garuda

Maruna appears to grudgingly respect his father and follow his wisdom. Yet he admits to not missing his father at all, implying that their relationship was not particularly warm.[2][22]

Vinata

Maruna seems to have cared about his mother and has admitted to missing her.[2] She seems to have warmly taught him and warned him about future perils, such as insight.[6] Yet after her death during the Cataclysm, Maruna shed no tears and claimed that one must accept things as they are.[25]

Akasha

As the currently highest ranking nastika of the clan, Maruna respects her greatly. He fully trusts that her decisions are what is best for the clan and subjects to them even if they would personally hurt him. Akasha seems to care about Maruna and lay her hopes for the future of the clan on his back.[25][26][14]

Rakshasas
Samphati

Samphati subjected Maruna to an extremely cruel training consisting of 4 years during which she constantly beat him up with only short breaks for her vigor to replenish.[25][28] She despises Maruna because his brother, Yuta, ate her sister, Yatayu. She wishes to harm Maruna and Kalavinka, hoping that this would make Yuta suffer, and only holds back because Akasha asked her to.[29] As such, she acts extremely coldly towards him, cuts off his attempts to strike conversation, and repeatedly gets angry whenever he calls Yuta by name.

Despite this, Maruna does not resent Samphati. Ever since first meeting her, he seems to admire her for her power and her demeanor. He considers how subjecting him to the training must be harming her, feels pity for her and attempts to better understand her situation.[28] He developed to 4th stage when aiming to protect her.[31] And when she is in a life-threatening situation, he thinks nothing of setting aside his pride and begging others to help.[7]

In season 3, he shows great remorse at being unable to protect Samphati and does what he can to learn of what befell her, clinging on to hope that she must be alive somewhere.[26] When Samphati reappears, it is revealed that she no longer harbors vengeful feelings towards Yuta and she is better able to express worry and caring concerning Maruna. Maruna appears to be protective of her and it has been suggested that he feels affection towards Samphati.[31][32]

Shakuntala

Maruna and Shakuntala were childhood friends, playing with each other since they were both at 2nd stage. Shakuntala clearly adores Maruna and always expresses joy at seeing him and looks forward when he is to visit. Regardless, she teases him about developing slower than her, since she hits both 3rd and 4th stage long before him despite being much younger.

Maruna often complains to her about his dissatisfaction with his situation. He also seems to listen to her and admits to missing her smile.[2][3]

Yuta

Maruna and Yuta care about each other greatly. Maruna was alone for centuries, so he was extremely happy to finally have siblings. He feels extremely protective of them and inspires them to believe in themselves.

Although Yuta was not well accepted in the clan, Maruna would always assure him that there is nothing wrong with him, that his mismatched wings are lovely, and that he is sure Yuta can get through all trials that await him, for they are brothers. When parting, Maruna even gifted Yuta with his sword. The siblings promised each other to stay strong, grow up, and meet once again. Both think of each other lovingly as they search for each other. This is a significant part of the motivation of both characters at the beginning of the story.

Once they reunite, Maruna and Yuta find themselves on different sides and with some major disagreements. Yuta has grown close to humans, befriended them even, while Maruna has killed many and thinks of them as little more than insects. Maruna expects that Yuta will listen to him and attempts to assume authority, but to his surprise, Yuta resists and they fight.[37][38]

Later on, they manage to meet and talk about their respective positions. Both express that they still care about one another and they agree to search for Kalavinka.[39][40][41] Maruna protects Yuta when Samphati attacks, but this forces Yuta to flee, preventing the brothers from further speaking.[39]

In season 3, Yuta interferes to prevent Leez Haias from killing Maruna, further affirming their bond.[42][43]

Kalavinka

Maruna and his little sister care about each other greatly. Before separating, they promised one another that they would stay strong and reunite once more. Finding her is one of Maruna's main motivations.[34][35] Though not only out of sentiment, but also because she might be carrying the power of the name.[41]

Shess

Maruna and Shess appear to get along well enough. Shess often teases Maruna, mainly about his young age, which Maruna attempts to defend against weakly.[16] Shess seems to be taking actions in Maruna's interests and is empathetic to his situation. Though Maruna does resort to threatening Shess at times,[46] he does appear to worry when seems to go badly for Shess.[47]

Pingara

Food! When Pingara was young, Maruna would hunt him. Thanks to Pingara's hiding transcendentals, he managed to escape, but he still has nightmares about it.[48] Therefore, he is extremely wary of Maruna and trusts him little. Maruna acknowledges Pingara's skills and considers them to be annoying. He threatens to eat Pingara same as his other clanmates.[8]

Riagara

Food! Snakes are Maruna's favorite meal.[8] Riagara hates Maruna for eating so many of her clanmates and she naturally fears him,[48] but she is able to smartly manipulate Maruna to do the dirty work for her on several occasions.[35][49]

Cloche

Snake! Delicious. Cloche is absolutely terrified of Maruna because he keeps threatening to eat her.[51] She envies him for his power and unique transcendental skill.[48]

Hura

Hura is too small to be considered a good meal.[52] Maruna mostly seems to ignore him and he seems to believe Hura is an idiot.[48] Yet Hura too manages to manipulate Maruna by having information that is crucial to him.[53] Hura is not scared of anyone or anything.

Gods
Kubera
Kubera has promised to help Maruna find his siblings if Maruna takes part in his plan and kills humans. Naturally, Maruna did not see through the manipulation and took the deal.[54] Although he witnesses as Kubera manipulates other people and even considers Kubera's actions to be extremely cruel,[4] he obeys until the very futility of his actions becomes obvious.[7]

Agni

As Maruna endangered cities and people Agni cared about, Agni originally thought extremely ill of Maruna and planned to make Maruna pay once he gets his hands on him.[56] Maruna, realizing that Agni was far stronger than him, feared the god and made effort to avoid him.[9][6]

In season 3, the scales shift and Agni cautiously accepts Maruna as an ally. Though he refrains from judging Maruna's actions, he makes it clear that Maruna is not forgiven.[57] Maruna seems to respect Agni.[58]

Humans/Halfs
Kasak Rajof

During their first encounter, Maruna and Kasak did not establish a good relationship, as Maruna managed to kidnap Kasak's daughter and tried to beat him up for information. Likewise, Kasak branded Maruna as a villain and did his best to kill him off.[60][61]

In season 3, they find themselves on the same sides and the relationship between them seems to have calmed down a lot. Still, Kasak does not appear to trust Maruna a refuses to reveal anything of importance.[58]

Ran Sairofe

They did not meet until season 3, when they are forced to go on a mission together.[63] At first, Maruna seems to mostly overlook Ran,[64] but as time passes, the two are able to joke and bicker.[58] They become curious about each other's circumstances and Maruna seems to be careful not to harm Ran even in threatening situations.[65]

Asha Rahiro

Since Maruna killed her mother, destroyed her whole village, and destroyed much of her home planet, Asha harbors deep resentment against Maruna.[66] This feeling, however, is not mutual. Although Maruna considers Asha to be a dangerous magician he should have killed on previous occasions, he makes no active effort to go after her.[67]

Leez Haias

Since Leez believed Maruna destroyed her village, she vowed revenge against him.[69] She displays deep hatred whenever he is mentioned, attempts to grow stronger so that she is able to fight him, and takes every opportunity to strike against him.[70][71]

This gets complicated by the fact that she falls in love with Maruna's brother, who tries to dissuade her from her path of revenge.[43] In season 3, she learns that Maruna did not, in fact, destroy her village, and struggles with whether to let go of her spite.[72]

Maruna has little respect for humans. He tries to kill Leez when their paths cross, but he seems to regard this as more of a task rather than something personal.[37] Once his orders lose value, he also loses reason to strike against her.[73]

Elwin Rakan

Since Maruna respects halfs of allied clans, unless he is following orders, he tries to avoid harming them. When Elwin was kidnapped and the Ananta clan suras wanted to feed her to Upanis,[75] Maruna volunteered to guard her instead and he let her go after the on-going attack was over.[76][77]

When they meet in season 3, Elwin recognizes him and displays fear, yet she warily accepts to help him.[15] Though Maruna attempts to hold her hostage to get hold of information about the Eye of Perishment, he also protects her from harm.[78]

Brilith Ruin
These two do not meet until season 3. Brilith immediately identifies Maruna as the rakshasa responsible for the deaths of so many humans and does not hesitate to attack him.[79] Even when he is accepted as an ally, Brilith is of the opinion that Maruna is a dangerous threat which should not have been left alive.[80] Maruna does not appear to have particular opinions about Brilith.

Parr Hael
As Parr witnessed Maruna killing many of her fighter friends, she hates him and calls for action to be taken against him.[81] She recognizes him when they meet in season 3 and expresses fear.[82][15] Maruna does not seem to care.

Kaz Lehn

Though Maruna did not think much of Kaz, Kaz managed to trick Maruna and get him into a position where he would have to make a sincere wish for the happiness of a human if he was to develop.[84][85] Kaz seems to have fear of Maruna, but it has been hinted that this may be an act.

Sagara is a nastika and the current king of the Ananta clan. How she became king is currently a mystery, as she lacks the support of the nastikas of her clan other than Vasuki. She is currently in the human realm looking to avenge the death of the first king, Ananta.

Appearance
Sagara's normal appearance is that a 14-year-old girl (15 Korean age), but will change it under special circumstances, such as appearing 20 for the purpose of romance.[3][4] Her complexion is pale. She has long blue hair that she has fastened into two side-ponytails. The ponytails are bound with red ties with a blue, leaf-like decoration attached to it. She has thin black eyebrows and red eyes with vertically elongated pupils. She also has pointy teeth and a purple tongue. Sagara wears wide gray short pants that are held up with galluses, with a large blue ribbon in the back. The galluses are fastened to the pants with red buttons in the front, and are tied in several layers around her neck, leaving her back bare. She wears a piece of blue cloth that goes around her bust, and is worn over the galluses. She wears purplish high-soled shoes that have a blue outline on the top, which is fastened by red rubber, and purplish stockings, that elongate into her pants. Leez's friend Kaz commented on how she was even more beautiful than Brilith. She also wears purplish gloves. On top of her usual garment, she often wears a lighter purplish sleeved overcoat. The overcoat is worn closed on the top, but widely opens in the lower part, which leaves her abdomen area visible. The coat comes with a wide blue scarf on the top, and fastens two red open-circles at the sharp ends of the coat on both sides.

In order to break the barrier that protects Brilith, she uses her transcendental Black Scale and partially transforms. She loses her coat, and has a purplish-black right arm that resembles a large claw with two large teeth on the outer side. The upper part of her arm has a crimson pattern on it, and her shoulder has a few crimson to purple feather-like objects on it. Her enlarged left arm is of similar purplish-black color and has five sharp claws tipping her fingers. The claw appears to have purplish bone formations around the wrist, thumb, index finger, ring finger and a red circle surrounding the base of thumb and index finger.

As a nastika, Sagara is capable of freely changing her gender, and she uses her stronger male form to deal with dangerous situations such as confronting Agni or Leez. As a male she has short blue hair, red eyes with elongated pupils, thin black eyebrows, and her clothes closely resemble what she wore in her female form. She wears dark purplish shoes, long trousers of similar color which are held up by a belt and lack the ribbon, and a purplish vest with a single red button. On top she wears her regular coat which comes with the scarf, but is lacking the red circles.

Personality
Sagara likes to manipulate those around her, and often has a mischievous smile while she does so. She's very assertive and willing to sacrifice anything to achieve her goals. She's also honest about herself such as admitting her selfishness as a king. If Sagara has also been shown to not care about the well-being of her clan despite being king due to her clan's nastikas not acknowledging her as the king as well as not looking for revenge on Ananta's death, she is shown being angry when her followers were hurt by Gandharva suras, and refused to let Riagara cover their escape from Agni since she would die doing so. She can usually keep her cool, and emerge with a smiling face when she is challenged, but dislikes it when her plans are interrupted, or when she is threatened by those much lower on the power ladder than her. Rank means a great deal to Sagara, who fixates on her proximity to power. She is also fond of creating havoc. Despite that, she also has a softer side and has been shown crying when Ananta died. Altogether, Sagara is a very emotional sura; whatever happens, she reacts heavily to it. Her appearance is very important for her, too. She likes to hear she's beautiful and dislikes taking her partial transformation because it makes her look ugly. It is hinted this is the reason she stays in female form, despite being a little stronger in her male form.

Sagara is one of the 12 characters who appear in the series Prologue. She shares a panel with Brilith and may represent "justice and responsibility."[6]
During Ananta's reign, Sagara was like his right hand [7]. Currygom has stated that if Sagara was stronger she might have been a great king because she knows how a king should be. [8]
Under the current rules applying to nastikas in the Human realm, Sagara is weaker than a rakshasa. [9]
Sagara has had "too many lovers and children to remember them all," but this is likely true for most nastikas.

Currygom says her female voice is very beautiful and in male form it is somewhat high.
In terms of the female characters with the most hair, Sagara holds second place. Only Taraka has more hair than her. [11][12]
In Hindi, "सागर" (Sagara) means sea.

History
Sagara is one of the weaker nastikas from the Ananta clan and she became the third king of the clan under unknown circumstances after something happened to Manasvin in between the years N5 and N15. [1]

However, she cannot be considered a legitimate king because most of the clan members do not recognize her as one due to her lack of power. Sagara was able to hold on to her position and keep her life because of the support Vasuki continuously provides to her.[2] With Sagara as king, the Ananta clan has grown weaker. They have been able to survive mainly because their greatest enemy, the Garuda clan, is also weakened due to their king being comatose.

Ananta was Sagara's first love but he never returned her affection. During her life, Sagara had loved other people but her feelings for Ananta remained even after his death. The sincerity of her love for Ananta is rather questionable because of her evident desire for a position of power.

Sagara has had quite an active romantic life fitting for someone who has lived for so long. Her relationships have lasted tens of millions of years and among her partners, her longest relationship was with Vasuki. Sagara stopped loving Vasuki long before breaking up with him. Riagara was born between them. Since approximately D400, Sagara started dating Manasvin until he disappeared.

Pingara is their offspring.

She has not dated anyone after Manasvin.

Sagara has had many other children, so many that she does not remember all of them. She only knows the names of a select few that were special to her.

For the purpose of resurrecting Ananta, Sagara is currently cooperating with suras from other clans and even with the god responsible for Ananta's death.

Sagara/Relationships

Nastikas

Manasvin

Manasvin and Sagara have been lovers for centuries by the beginning of the story (~600 years)[1] and they had a child together.[2] She was his right-hand person and advisor during his time as king.[3]

Manasvin's love for Sagara is patient and selfless. He admires her brutal honesty [4] and is willing to put her desires first, even if this would mean that she would leave him for another lover or in pursuit of power.

Sagara appears to recognize the depth of his love, however, she is willing to leave him for a position of greater power when the opportunity presents itself. Thankfully, the need does not arise.[5]

Sagara shares many of Manasvin's opinions, including his contempt for hypocrites and devotion to Ananta and their clan.[4] The current state of their relationship is unknown as Manasvin's situation remains unexplained.

Vasuki

Sagara and Vasuki's romance has been her longest relationship. Their only known child is Riagara. They broke up long before D400. [6]  Sagara quickly moved on because she no longer loved him. For Vasuki —who still loves her deeply until this day— Riagara became his only reason to continue living.

Vasuki's love for Sagara is devoted, selfless, and supportive. He puts her feelings and dreams first, even if they are not together. [6] He cares for her happiness. Vasuki is the only reason none of the other Ananta nastikas dare murder Sagara to become king themselves. [7]

Sagara scorns Vasuki by calling him a coward because she thinks that Vasuki abandoned Ananta to his death. Regardless, she still worries about him. 

Rakshasas

Riagara

Riagara is the daughter of Sagara and Vasuki and she was raised by the latter after the couple broke up. Riagara adores her mother and is one of her most loyal followers though their relationship is quite formal and they do not openly display any affection. Nevertheless, Sagara has shown concern towards her a couple of times.[10] Sagara communicates her plans directly to Riagara, who is the leader of the Ananta rakshasas.[7][11] She also seeks out her daughter to consult her plans and vent when things are going wrong.[12] Riagara is happy when Sagara praises her for her ability to improvise and adapt when their plans take unexpected turns.[5]

At the end of season 2, Sagara vanishes from existence alongside Riagara and Pingara.[5] After their return seven years later, their relationship has a very different dynamic. Riagara loses her position of right-hand after Sagara gathers a new group of suras.[13] Sagara no longer communicates anything to her and now Riagara expresses doubts and concern regarding her mother's plan. [14] [15] She feels constantly left out because she did not acquire any knowledge from the records of Time unlike Sagara and Pingara.[16]

Pingara proclaims that Sagara feels no love for the child of a former lover, and as such Riagara expresses her desire for affection through fierce loyalty. [16] Those words get to Riagara and lead her to make a mistake that causes the loss of Pingara in Mistyshore.[17] Sagara punishes her by isolating her from the rest of the group.[18]

Pingara

Note: Pingara's gender is unknown. The pronouns he/him/his will be used to refer to Pingara.

Pingara is the child of Sagara and Manasvin and was raised by them in the Sura realm. Sagara does not have an intimate relationship with him as they barely exchange any words and none of them seems particularly worried about the other. Pingara follows Sagara but is constantly questioning her decisions, though never to her face.

Following the events of N16, they spent 7 years in a state of non-existence that allowed them to learn information about the future. This event did not have a big impact on how they treat each other. However, it helped Pingara to accept Ananta's resurrection without further questioning.[14]


Pingara sacrifices himself in Riagara's place in Mistyshore. Thinking that he will perish soon, in his last words, he urges his mother to remember what his father used to say about not trusting the gods. For the very first time, Sagara shows sentiment towards Pingara. She sheds tears and is visibly angry at Riagara for the loss of her youngest child. [17]  Sagara seems to think that Pingara is gone but the rakshasa is being held captive.[20]

Cloche & Clophe

The twins might be children that Sagara fathered with a rakshasa but it has yet to be confirmed. The children were raised by an older brother in the Human realm. Sagara's relationship with both of them is contrasting.

Cloche holds Sagara in high esteem and is fairly loyal to her. Sagara seeks out Cloche as her confidante when Riagara is absent.[4] Sagara does not get angry when Cloche is forced to disclose their plans but is displeased when she does so carelessly.[22] Cloche is constantly worrying about Sagara's safety and is always against letting her put herself in danger.[23]


Cloche is one of the Anantas that went with Sagara to aid the Gandharva clan in N5.

With Clophe, Sagara's interactions are nonexistent. He is not very loyal to her and only follows her because of Cloche. They do not speak to each other. Sagara respects Clophe's rule of exclusively speaking to his sister. [24] He has an interest in the humans that Sagara is unaware of.

Despite their cold relationship, Clophe worries about his king's well-being [25] and Sagara notices if he is absent. [17]

Hura

Note: Hura has no gender, but the pronouns he/him/his will be used to refer to Hura.

Hura is the only rakshasa the Asura clan sent to support Sagara in her plans. However, Hura carefully follows his own agenda unnoticed by anyone. [26] Their relationship is strictly professional, and Sagara does not have any ill feelings against him as she does with Tatia and Chatan.[27]

Sagara thinks of Hura as a tool she can continue using even after the alliance with the Asura clan has broken. [28] Nevertheless, Hura is the one who has the upper hand. He has been manipulating Sagara and her lackeys from the shadows.[18] Hura has an interest in making Cloche and Clophe drift away from Sagara.

Tatia and Chatan

These are some of the new allies that Sagara has brought in season 3. Both are going against their clan's will by supporting Sagara. The nastika has aversion towards them because their clan either supported killing Ananta or did nothing to prevent it.[31] Sagara does not speak much with either of them, but she has worked closely with Chatan.[32] It would seem that Sagara chose to overlook Chatan's disobeying of her orders in Mistyshore.[33]

Chatan and Tatia do not harm humans and they do everything they can to avoid it. This kind of attitude upsets Sagara to the core. She demands full commitment, and makes it clear that she is willing to throw them away for this hypocritical mercy.

Brilith Ruin

The immense insecurity Sagara feels about her power status in the Ananta clan surfaces as soon as she learns of Brilith's position as a priestess. She loathes her.[7]

Sagara's shrewdness and the mind games she uses to manipulate people are futile when it comes to Brilith. She always loses in their confrontations because the priestesses' determination infuriates her. Once that happens, Sagara acts very impulsively and becomes oblivious to the long-term consequences of her actions.[8] Sagara is particularly vulnerable to Brilith's gaze.[35]

Sagara develops an obsession with Brilith after reading about her true identity in the records of Time.[36]

Awakened Brilith knows Sagara very well from many of her past lives in which the nastika caused her a lot of pain. She hates Sagara like any other nastika and thinks that she will never change her nasty habits.

During his competition for the next Priest of the Earth, the king had a dream that someone of sura blood would cause him trouble. He decided to only allow the purebloods to continue. God Kubera, showing up at the scene, asks the king whether Indra commanded the death of his knights, but he denies that Indra had anything to do with it. Kubera deduces it is a higher god from his insight and leaves him.

When Enan's friend begins attacking the palace with her fiendish magic, the king's men go to stop her. Indra tells the Daksha that many will die unless he denounces fiendish magic entirely. Furthermore, Indra promises to reveal the culprit behind the lightning incident, the death of the king's family, as well as what is going on at the moment, provided the king obeys. He would go on to accept this deal.

Manasa was Ananta's mate at the Beginning of the universe and the one wielding the power to go against 'time.' Only Visnu chose to help him at first, but with only fragments of Manasa's soul and fractured name left that are now incompatible with each other, he combined forces with Brahma to create two new creatures: Manasvin, who carries what is left of Manasa's name, and Sagara, who carries what is left of Manasa's soul.

Anna Haias is a pure-blood human and the mother of Kubera Leez. In the first two seasons of the webtoon, Anna's fate remains unknown.

Appearance
Anna is a woman with yellowish tanned skin, dark-green hair, dark-green eyebrows, and light-green eyes. Her daughter Kubera last sees her wearing a long pinkish sleeved dress with a grayish-black apron on-top of it.

Personality
Anna appears to have a cheerful and caring personality. She does not mind her daughter sleeping in late, and seems to approach situations in a restful, motherly way. In her younger days, she had many half friends.[1]

Notes
Anna shares her last name with Eline Haias, Ran Sairofe's aunt, and Ping Haias, a former classmate of Ran's. Their relationships are currently unknown.
Plot

History
In a flashback, young Leez looks at a photo of her parents taken on the 10th day of the 10th month in the year D995,[2] which was Anna's 19th birthday. This was the year that Rao won the Fighter Championship, and he gave the gold medal shown in the photo to Anna as a birthday present.[3]

In the same flashback, Anna is shown folding clothes when Kubera asks her when her dad will be coming home. Anna replies that it will be when she is a little older.[2] It is very likely that this conversation happened before the events in the year N5 when Rao went missing from the transport ship from planet Carte,[2] and when Anna reportedly died.[4]

When Gandharva asks Kubera Leez for her name upon their first meeting, she recalls Anna advising her at a very young age to never tell her name to outsiders, claiming her name was special.[5]

Anna appears in another flashback wearing a blue dress and apron and holding a broom, trying to sweep leaves, but is interrupted by Roen Renod, who excites a young Kubera. Anna tells her daughter that she was a fighter in her youth, and had many half friends at the time.[1]

Leda Halo is a pure-blood human who works for Mirha Simon as her Personal Assistant at the Temple of Wind in Aeroplateau.

Appearance
Leda appears to be a woman at about average height, with short, reddish brown hair and dark, slanted eyes. Her usual attire is that of a dark business suit.

Personality
Leda seems very businesslike as well as punctual, seeing as she dislikes it when Mirha is late. Being Mirha's personal assistant, Leda seems to care greatly about Mirha's well-being, and usually does things as per Mirha's instruction. However, when it comes to matters Leda feels strongly about, it seems that Leda can and will use her own judgement over Mirha's: as seen when she gave Leez Mirha's research papers,[1] despite Mirha saying that she only wanted to show them to Leez after Asha's trial was resolved.[2]

Skills and Abilities
Not much is known yet about her skills other than being able to cast bhavati kubera and teaching the spell to Leez.[3]

Plot
Season 2
Chapter 29: Isle of Myths
(1) Leda hands Mirha a data sheet filled with personal information on Leez Haias. She then asks Mirha if she will really cooperate with Saha, considering Mirha and Asha were friends back on planet Carte. Mirha responds that it was really a one-sided friendship on her part, then says she will be heading out. This prompts Leda to ask if she really wants to and if she needs any help. Mirha tells her that it wasn't necessary, and that she is  getting used to her new legs. Mirha also wants to catch up on some recent events that she has apparently missed.

(5) Leda informs Mirha of how, as per Mirha's instructions, she tried to contact various temples, guilds, and academies where Leez and Asha had been; starting from Atera, as that was the first place Asha had visited with Leez. There was no response yet from the temple, but she did receive information from the guild and one of the academies, which revealed that Asha had been keeping Leez isolated in Atera, concealed from the outside world. Asha had also instructed the guild and temple employees to not talk about the red sky incident to the girl, using the excuse that she was too young to hear about a disaster like that. Mirha realizes that the information Asha was trying to conceal was not the red sky incident, but the last few people Leez knew.

(6) When Leez and Asha visit the Temple of Wind, Leez is visibly amazed by the beautiful gardens, saying that they must be difficult to maintain. Leda tells her that gardening is Mirha's hobby, and that with a single use of bhavati vayu she trims the trees and sweeps up the mess. Leda then leads them all inside, where Mirha then tells Leez that Leda will teach her bhavati kubera, and the two of them go outside.

Chapter 30: Falling Petals
(1) Leda tutors Leez on how to use bhavati kubera. Leda is curious as to how Leez managed to learn the spell on her own, and expresses that in order to teach Leez, she needs to know what mistakes are being made. Leez is reluctant to tell Leda at first; however, due to her desperation to learn the spell, she reveals how she had repeatedly jumped off a cliff to master it, and swears Leda to secrecy.

Mirha notes that though she was aware of Leez's great strength, she was not aware of her impressive cognitive and memorization skills. Leda feels that Leez should know the truth of what she, too, is involved in, but Mirha wants Leez to gain some emotional distance from Asha so that the truth would hurt her less. However, Leda still has her doubts concerning the defense of Asha at the trial as well as allowing Asha and Leez to associate without intervention.

Rao Leez is a pure-blood and the father of Kubera Leez. He was the first owner of the god-level item the Neutral Bow. He disappeared from a rescue transport en route from Planet Carte to Planet Willarv in the year N5, at the age of 29; he is presumed dead.

His marriage with Anna Haias was not a formal one,[2] and the fact that they had a daughter was only known to his best friend (a fighter) and the local villagers.

Rao was the one who gave his daughter the name "Kubera," which is the name she was known by in her village. Sometimes the villagers also called her "Leez," after her father.

Rao is one of the leading forces in the world of Kubera; clues about him will gradually be revealed.

Appearance
Rao is a tall young man with lightly tanned skin tone. He has short, curly, messy, light blue-green hair, and wears brownish-gray sports-suit in the photo in which he appears.[3] In another flashback, Rao wears a white long-sleeved shirt, blue trousers, and black shoes.[4]

Personality

He was seen as reckless man who threw himself in the gravest dangers, unconcerned with value of his own life. One can call him irresponsible for leaving his pregnant wife to set off to Carte, or too dedicated in his desire to help others.[5]

According to Ran Sairofe, Rao ate well, slept well, laughed well, he had a trusting personality, he lept into danger with no hesitation and without knowing the value of life.[6]

According to Vayu, Rao would deceive himself in order to maintain his vigor, to the point that others became unable to see him for who he is. Rao felt that he does not belong, and his life was lonely.[7]

Skills and Abilities
Rao was a strong fighter, the victor of the fighters championship of D995[8], and a man acknowledged even by suras and gods for his skills.[9]

Although he was a pureblood human, he was able to use transcendental skills. He could use magic without calculations and god-level items.[6] He had the ability to rise to the top of a cliff in one step[10] and he was gifted the Neutral Bow, one of the most powerful god-level items ever created.[11]

Autobiography
Rao has a biography, "How I Survived: Autobiography of Rao Leez, the Final Champion."[12] However, it was not written by him, but by many of his fans and peers, and is considered somewhat unreliable for that reason. Many who see the book for the first time think it really is about "survival," but it is about his fights. It is full of praise about him from the beginning to the end, with the intent to instill awe into the reader. Nevertheless, it was a bestseller. Because of Rao's high popularity, all items advertised under his name sold like crazy—even books. (Some others like Mr.Kasak were popular as well, but Rao's popularity still surged because of people going like "How..? He's a pure-blood human?!", totally surprised.)

Because of his nature of rarely refusing requests, Rao often made appearances at advertising festivals; but he was often very busy, so companies just gave him clothes. Everything he wore instantly became popular.[2]

Notes
Rao Leez won the Fighter Championship in year D995. He gave the gold medal he received to Anna as a birthday present.[8]
Since he was really popular, all products advertised under his name easily sold out. Ran once received fighting gear as a birthday present, and he happily applauded "because it was advertised by Rao Leez."[13]
The Neutral bow fell to earth (Willarv) when Rao disappeared from the transport from Carte.

Plot

History

Rao Leez was a skilled fighter and magician from Willarv, and the father of Kubera Leez.

He achieved so much while he was still young, that little more remained for him to accomplish.[3] He won a fighters championship in D995[8] and he was renowned not only among humans, but also among suras and gods.[9]

Rao secretly got married to another fighter, Anna Haias, but while she was pregnant, he left for the planet Carte.[6] The Cataclysm of N0 made it impossible for him to return and so he was still on Carte when disaster struck and the planet was all but destroyed. He was on board the last transport ship from Carte to Willarv[3] and he was granted the Neutral bow by god Vayu on this occasion,[11] but circumstances made it so that he had to sacrifice himself in order for the ship to land.[14]

And so, no one has ever heard of him since N5 and he never got the chance to see his daughter.[6] Regardless, he seems to have a strong influence over all those he interacted with, especially Asha Rahiro whose actions seemed to be tied to his fate and wishes.

Appearance
Lorraine appears as a woman with slightly tanned skin tone. She has dark-brown hair which she ties in a short ponytail on her back, and brown eyebrows. She wears a pair of round glasses. Unlike most other people, Lorraine seems to change her clothes often; though she tends to dress for comfort and not fashion. Both she and her cousin Siera have gold eyes, which is atypical for pureblood humans who generally have the same hair and eye color.

Personality
Lorraine appears to be a slightly playful and quite witty person, who holds responsibilities in high regard (except for the Priest of Creation position—see below). She can easily turn most situations in her favor, and often approaches situations calmly and logically. She seems to be quite difficult to surprise, and even if she is it doesn't often show. She is not very capable in physical terms. Lorraine also shows moderate interest in Asha, although she never displays an obsession like Ruche and Airi. She is also shown to be a very supportive mentor, exemplified by her enthusiasm to take on Asha as a student in her younger days[1] as well as her current treatment of Eiraheeari Catroshife.[2]

Lorraine was supposed to become the Priest of Creation before she ran away, leaving the responsibility to Lutz Sairofe.

Notes
Lorraine is from a wealthy family, and due to the nature of her magic she is an affluent person herself. She is rumored to donate money from the sale of her merchandise for improvement in the Fighters' welfare.[3]
Due to her Fighter obsession, she prefers muscular men but her fiance is not one. As a result, Lorraine has been postponing her actual marriage for years.

History
In the year D989 the families of Saha On, age 30, and Lorraine, age 10, arranges their marriage. Ten years later, in a diner in Eloth, Lorraine tells Saha that she still does not think about marriage, but she is unwilling to break off their engagement for now because it would cause problems with their families. She reveals to him that she prefers masculine men who are more accomplished and so he resolves to accept several high-ranking positions he was recently offered. Lorraine thinks to herself that if she waits long enough and gets too old for him, he will break off the engagement himself and find someone younger.[4]

Currygom once mentioned a love triangle in her me2day (now closed) between Lorraine, Saha, and Lutz Sairofe during their university days.[5]

Lorraine has met Laila Hemawati in her past, and the latter told her about Asha's unbelievable calculative powers and divine affinity.[6]

Rana Reimia is a pureblood and a magician of Mistyshore. She is a professor at the Mistyshore University of Magic.

Appearance
Rana appears to be a young woman, with light skin tone. She has long blue hair that she ties in a ponytail, blue eyebrows, and blue eyes. When she is first introduced, she is wearing blueish-gray shoes, a grayish medium-length skirt, and a green short-sleeved shirt. She often carries a book or a notebook with her. Through-out the story, Rana displays a wide wardrobe of outfits. Most are decently concealing and often include skirts or dresses. From season 3, Rana begins to wear a hat to hide the god-level item she is wearing on her head.

Personality
Rana initially appears as a cheerful and enthusiastic child. Becoming older, and being often around Ran seems to have made her more serious, although she sometimes still shows her childish side. She appears to be quick to anger, and often responds to Ran's stupidity in a physically harmful way. She seems to like studying, and appears to idolize Asha for her achievements. She is concerned with the fact that she's aging twice as fast as Ran, and that someday she'll be too old for him.

Notes and Trivia
Rana is one of the 12 characters that appear in the webtoon Prologue.[1]
Rana was the person that treated Ran's injuries from his fight with the Gandharva suras outside of Mistyshore's barrier.[2]
She likes mango milk and is touched by the fact that Ran actually left her a goodbye letter.[3]
She tells Ran to never use the skill that he used in his magic test ever again, as it may kill him.[4]
Rana is the person Ran likes, but they try to distance themselves from each other because of their age differences as a pureblood human and a Quarter.
Rana won beauty contests in N7, N8, and N9.[5]
Rana is a silent magic user.[6]
Plot
History

Rana was orphaned at a young age[7] and she spent part of her childhood on Taitalika before moving to Willarv.[8] Because of her triple resurrection attributes, high divine affinity, and good grasps of the mechanics of time logic, she was a rising star on Willarv with great potential.[9]


In D999, when she was 10 years old, she first met Ran Sairofe, who was 20 (age of appearance 10) at the time, and she fell in love at first sight.[10] Or rather when she heard his voice for the first time.[11] She helped him cope with the loss of his parents during the Cataclysm of N0 and knows the truth of what happened.[12][13]

By N2 she started giving private lessons to Ran who struggled with many subjects.[14] She passed her magic exam in Mistyshore partnered up with Ran, who apparently used some sort of special skill that uses up lifespan to protect Rana, which resulted in a high score for the exam.[4]

Rana also won beauty contests in N7, N8, and N9.[15] In N10, she was suggested as a possible marriage candidate for Saha On, but refused.[16][17] Due to her academic successes, she was a university student at 19, associate professor by the age of 22, and full professor by 26.

Rana was also a fan of Asha Rahiro.[19] She feared to confess to Ran because she worried that she would get old and ugly before him and he would not like her and she was not certain about his feelings.[15] She eventually made a deal with Eline Haias that if she can get Ran to graduate and get engaged to him, Eline would give her an item that prevents aging.[20]

Special Episode 2 - Terms of affection

In the 11th month of the year N7, Rana and Lutz are relaxing on a beach in Mistyshore while Ran is out swimming, and they discuss things entirely unrelated to academics, politics, or romance. Wondering if brothers might have similar preferences, Rana asks Lutz what kind of girls he likes. The description Lutz gives mostly matches Rana, what with being smart and a teacher, except for the fact that Lutz's perfect lady is supposed to have soft ears that perk up when surprised.


Rana reads a book which states that it is common for Yaksha halfs and quarters to be attracted to body parts resembling Yakshas, and that this preference is hereditary. Just as Rana realizes that even if Ran felt that way, his current phobia of halfs would have changed his approach, Ran runs to her, asking her to save him from a group of halfs. The onlookers mock him for this behavior.

In the 5th month of N16 when Rana just got alerted that Leez has awoken, Ran comes running, fearful of a group of nearby halfs, and hugs Rana. Once Rana points out that the halfs are gone, Ran self-deprecates himself for letting his fear influence his life so strongly. Rana assures him that all is well and Ran gives her a kiss on the cheek. This flusters Rana strongly because she worries what the people who are watching may think. Ran teases her and Rana shoos him away.

Mirha delivers a box that arrived for Rana from Eline. Rana and Ran then discuss the contents - an item which prevents aging. Ran warns Rana about the inconvenience of being unable to take off the item at any time and assures her that he does not mind if she ages more quickly than him, but Rana worries about the opinions of other people.


When she opens the box and witnesses the item, she begins to reconsider. Seeing the item, Ran blushes intensely and gets a nosebleed - the item is a headband with pink kitty ears. It would seem that the book was correct that Yaksha quarters are drawn to body parts resemblant of Yakshas.

Ran wonders about what Eline must have looked like in those kitty ears since he cannot even imagine this considering her serious personality. Apparently she got rid of all the photos from before she got married.

Rana considers that aging together naturally must be nice and she can understand the choice Eline made when she stopped wearing the item. However, achieving the same would be difficult for her and Ran because they age differently. When Ran asks what is on her mind, she tells him to find a way to age faster.

Although they have been traveling to all of Willarv's most attractive destinations in the following years to make up for the flop, the memory of the south pole remains the strongest.

Appearance
Airi appears to be a young woman with a light skin tone. She has long purple hair that she initially keeps in round shapes on the sides of her head and covered by hair accessories. Her eyebrows are of similar purplish color and her eyes are purple as well. She is wearing dark-purple high heeled boots, dark-purple short pants and a dark-purple cloth around her bust. On top of her dark-purple garment she wears a medium length lighter-purple skirt, that has two strips of cloth in the front that go over her chest and around the back of her neck.

In Season 2, she wears a short white dress resembling a cheongsam with black accents on the collar and sleeves; this particular outfit is from Lorraine Rartia.[1] She styles her hair in a bun secured with a black ribbon and wears red flats.

In Season 3, Airi wears a white off the shoulder halter-style dress. The long, loose sleeves of the dress extend into finger gloves. The skirt of the dress reaches her ankles and is slit up to the hip on the left side, where it is secured with a black belt. Underneath the dress she wears black leggings and black flats. Most of her hair is tied up in a large bun, with two small braids extending from behind her ears. The rest of her hair is worn down and reaches just past her shoulders.

Personality
Airi appears to have a fast-paced personality, and seems to prefer actions over words. She seems to hold Asha Rahiro in high regards; so does Ruche Seiran, and they can easily start fighting, often by physical means, over Asha. She is quick to act when she or her friends' lives are threatened, and shows little fear of her opponents. She does not seem to follow rules very well, and is an equal match to Lorraine in terms of wits.

Skills and Abilities
Airi is an A+ ranked magician. She has proven to be a very skilled fighter, since she has survived a fight with a rakshasa. She consistently beats Lorraine in fights despite Lorraine being two ranks above her. Asha's rank falls in between, despite having the highest test scores ever received without even taking the barrier portion of the magician's test. As a result, Airi's complaint that "They place all the AA rank magicians at the top, without regard to actual ability!" might hold some truth, and she may be stronger than her official rank implies.

One of her specialties is her fusion spell hoti asvins hoti kubera, which is enhanced by her birth attributes. It produces a swirling green light effect similar to the Regeneration transcendental of the Golden Knight, but its true effects are still unknown other than it provides quick healing from massive injuries.[2]

Notes
She writes in an exchange diary with her brother Claude.[3] According to a picture in her diary, she met with Agwen Rajof, Kasak Rajof, and Taksaka (wearing Visnu's earings) in D995, but does not remember it. She apparently suffered from amnesia during the N0 Cataclysm and is unable to remember some events from before it happened.[4] The reason for her apparent loss of memory is explained in Season 3 (see Plot section below).[5]
Her brother aided Laila Hemawati in the defense of Rindhallow—at least before he ran away—as Maruna and Gandharva gathered inferior suras preparing to attack the city.
Teo Rakan holds a grudge against Airi, seemingly for defeating her multiple times in the yearly Fighter Championship.[6] Throughout Season 2, it remains unknown if Airi reciprocates. The true reason for Teo's anger towards her is revealed in Season 3 (see Plot section below).
According to Airi's blog profile, she was born only three months after her brother. Currygom stated on her blog that the age difference is in fact correct, and will be mentioned later in the story.[7] It is finally explained in Season 3 (see Plot section below).[5]
Both Claude and Airi often leave their room wearing pajamas. Currygom has stated that one of the siblings usually buys pajamas for both of them. [8]

He has a reputation for not taking his job very seriously, which frustrates some of the other priests, especially Laila Hemawati.

Appearance
Claude appears as a young man with long, purple hair and purple eyes, similar to his sister Airi. He also wears glasses. When outdoors, he is usually shown wearing a fluffy green cape over a long, darker green jacket, with a matching fluffy green bucket hat.

Personality
He is the person with the least work for someone of his rank. Compared to Rindhallow's Priest of Darkness, Laila Hemawati, he is someone with too much free time. He often leaves his priest duties to priest candidates to go traveling, which really makes Laila mad. It would not be a problem if they could simply replace him with a priest candidate when he goes traveling; however, his magic ranking is overwhelming among triple-deaths, so he gets to remain a priest.

He has a serious case of brother complex and keeps an exchange diary with his sister Airi.[2] Each sibling possesses his or her own diary. Separate transmission equipment is not needed; instead, each diary simply sends information to the other when a page is filled up with a certain number of characters. It is an expensive but useful item. The information vanishes after a period of time, which is rather inconvenient.

Skills and Abilities
At the beginning of the story, he is one of the four existing AA-ranked magicians. Because of the nature of death magic, no matter how talented one is, many cannot adapt. However, it is no exaggeration to say that Claude was born for death magic, and can use it freely. This causes anxiety for people, and makes them reluctant to approach him, especially considering that hoti yama and the Marut spells are the spells most suited for murder.[3] According to Asha Rahiro, a Death spell cast by Claude can be said to be absolute, since he is 2nd-ranked among all magicians, and the only way a hoti yama spell can be undone is to have it cast on the subject again by a magician with equivalent or higher divine affinity than the original caster.[4]

He is known to carry around a deck of tarot-like cards for the purpose of fortune-telling. He claims that his predictions are pretty accurate, but Siera Sies, the Priest of Earth, complains that he never predicts anything positive.[5]

Laila Hemawati frequently uses Claude as a test subject for her experiments; he does this job willingly.[8]

Plot

History
Claude and his sister Airi Yui, were born in foreign parts. [17] Airi was formerly his older sister, and she died in the year D995 at the age of 12. [17] [18] Claude asked Eline Haias to resurrect Airi, but she refused.

Claude was 13 years old when he almost died during the Cataclysm. [18] At that time, Eline Haias and a hooded god approached him. Claude thought they had come to aid him, and as his lifespan will have ended in one month, he expressed the wish for his deceased sister to be returned to life. The god agreed to resurrect his sister as she was the day before her death, although Eline took credit for the resurrection. Eline also contacted the people who knew the siblings to change their origin story. The god additionally extend Claude’s lifespan by 200 years, so he could serve the god to repay his debt. [17] According to the cover story that Claude and his sister were to go along with, they were fraternal twins, but he was born three months earlier. Since then, he has been the older sibling. [18]


Claude could use silent magic since he was very young; he allegedly had a wretched childhood. [17] His mastery in silent magic has earned him the position of one of the strongest magicians in Willarv. Though Claude is the Priest of Death, he does not carry out his duties seriously. He constantly slacks off and delegates all the work to the priest candidates.[19] Many people dislike his behavior and want to replace him, but he maintains his position because he is the best in death magic, though he would be apparently delighted to step down.[20]

He met Laila Hemawati when he was a child; they used to have a sort of teacher-student relationship. [21] As a fellow priest of Rindhallow, Laila is constantly forcing him to do his job, and quick to physically punish him when he neglects it. [20] [22] During his adult life, he has taken action to protect her life.

The hooded god discloses to Claude that in the past, it was possible to revive a person with their true soul. But that changed when a nastika started to annihilate those souls. [31] The gods decided to protect the human souls by modifying the process. Claude retorts that a resurrected person still has their memories and habits, to him, they are not fake. The hooded god clarifies that those concepts have nothing to do with the soul. The god adds that the soul contains only the strongest of memories. Claude listens carefully to the explanation, but he still stands by his beliefs. He is convinced that the can love a revived person as much as he formerly did.

After hearing this, the hooded god agrees to resurrect his sister as she was the day before her death, and Claude is not to divulge this. Synopsis
Ari first appears in chapter 27 where he is talking with Airi about Lorraine's delayed package. Unable to calm Airi, he is left alone to guard the package just in front of Lorraine's shop. Once the package gets stolen, he quickly gets a person with a loudspeaker to announce the theft, and starts to loudly cry when no-one steps forward to catch the thieves. This softens Leez's heart, who decides to give chase.

Eiraheeari later visits Brilith with Lorraine, he bows before the Oracle, and appears amazed, after hearing her story about the Staff of Agni. They return to Lorraine's shop with the weapon, and he appears quite shocked about finding the supposed to be guarding Airi sleeping instead. He quickly grows wary of the battle of wits that ensues between Lorraine and Airi, and lashes out by shouting for them to stop. He continues talking in a peaceful manner, and is surprised along with Lorraine and Airi by the red glowing sky.

He is allowed to come along, as Lorraine and Airi prepare to leave for the palace with a flying device. He is fastened to the machine by a chain, but he is completely unprepared for the acceleration as they take off, causing him to fall off and hang by his left ankle as they fly. He is about to be saved by Sagara who notices them, grabs him and is about to bring him safely onto the machine, but drops him. As Lorraine and Airi leave him with Sagara as they flee , he is left hanging from the floating machine. Once the attack on Atera is over, he finally manages to draw Lorraine's attention and is saved from his predicament.

Ari is from Isholy, his parents came to Willarv briefly on business before the Cataclysm and brought him along, but they died during the N0 Cataclysm, so Ari is all alone now because all his relatives are from Isholy. Briefly he was taken under the care of Saha On, the President of the Eloth Magic Guild, but Lorraine took him as disciple because of his triple Brahma attributes. Unlike Ran who had a Half parent and a pureblood parent, the previous five generations of Ari's ancestry were all quarters, so he's too far removed from the original sura blood. As a result, his physical abilities are almost the same as a pureblood's, the only thing distinguishing him as a quarter is his slower aging.

Laila has the physical appearance of a woman in her early 30's. She has pale skin, long, white, straight hair, purple eyes, and a mole under her left eye. She does not wear make-up[3]; although, she often wears purple lipstick to match her eyes. If Laila had not worn her mask, she would have gotten a very dark tan.[3] She wears her hair up under the mask to not give away anything about her physical appearance. She also has ripped abdominal muscles.[4]

Her wardrobe includes a variation of sleeved robes of different colors (black, brown, purple, dark blue, and green). The robes usually cover her whole body, but some of them reveal her shoulders. She wears black or purple long gloves all the time. She wears a pair of boots or flats; she used to wear heels. [5] Sometimes she also wears a black cloak.

Personality
Laila has a serious and calculative personality; she suppresses her emotions, and even when fully prepared to vent them, she retains her composure and dignity. [6] [1] [7] Claude said that in the past Laila used to be sentimental and cried for deceased animals. [8]

As a priestess, she possesses an immense sense of duty to the point that she is willing to bury her grudges to protect Rindhallow. [9] Laila is frank and speaks her mind even if she has to contradict a god's opinion. [10] She is greatly respected as a priestess and magician.

Laila values human lives [11], which she proved by choosing to preserve a life instead of getting valuable information. [12] Laila would also worry about the well-being of a rakshasa. [13] She seems unforgiving with people who have killed others even though they were not in control of themselves [6] or were unaware of the situation. [1] Laila refuses to have her life dictated by others and to submit to expectations. She will fight to secure her place and her survival. [14][1] [7]

Laila often gets irritated with Claude's lack of commitment to his position as the Priest of Death; she is constantly forcing him to do his job [15] [16]. She is quick to physically punish him when he neglects his job or when he steps out of line. [17] She also has very little patience for Claude's false politeness. [8] [2]

Skills and Abilities
Laila is one of the strongest magicians on Willarv. She specializes in Chandra magic due to her attributes, but she is also proficient in other types of magic, such as hoti Vayu. [18] Her mental strength and good judgment in dire situations is among her more valuable assets, which she receives praise for. [2] [14]

Her mastery in silent magic has earned her the recognition as the leading expert in dream-tracking.[19] According to a god, such mastery in her skill was uncommon even among those of the ancient human race. [14]

As a quarter, Laila possesses superior physical strength which gives her an edge as a fighter. She often displays her martial abilities against Claude Yui. [15] [16] She is skilled with weapons, particularly the spear, and in fighter tournaments, she prefers to fight with a spear than using magic. [20] She won the N19 Fighter Championship against Teo Rakan, although god Chandra rigged the tournament in her favor. [10] [14]

Laila has an interest in conducting experiments. She also teaches several lectures at the Rindhallow Magic University.

Notes
A talking alarm clock with Laila's image is seen waking up Rana in Mistyshore.
The name on Gandharva's stolen magician's license was "Roi Hemawati." It's unknown if he's related to Laila.[21]
Laila means "night" in Hebrew and Arabic.
Laila frequently uses Claude as a test subject for her experiments; he does this job willingly.[22]
During season 3, Chandra makes Laila assist him while he bathes. Currygum clarified that Laila was like a personal attendant like those of the medieval times. [23]
Laila appears as one of the vague silhouettes that Brilith recalls when Agni asked her if she had a reason to continue living.

Plot

History
Laila’s real name is Kubera Hemawati. When she was a child, she received an oracle from god Chandra. He told her to cover her face and forget her true name, and if doing so did not change her destiny, to call for him. [25] Since then, she has lived under the alias "Laila" and covered her face with a giant green monster mask.

Laila was a priestess candidate in the Temple of Darkness before the Cataclysm, and her mentor was the Priestess of Darkness. She was deeply attached to her mentor. The Priestess summoned god Chandra during the Cataclysm to protect Rindhallow. However, he was unaware of the changes in the summoning rules, so he overused his powers, consuming the lifespan of his summoner. [6] [1] Laila was present when her mentor died and witnessed as the god uttered cruel words on behalf of his summoner. He also blamed Laila for her mentor's death because she should have been the one to summon him. Before returning to the god realm, Chandra stated that she will have no alternative but to call him soon, and he also promised that she would not die like her mentor. Laila profoundly resents Chandra for the death of her mentor. [1] She became the new Priestess of Darkness.

Laila was childhood friends with Jibril Ajes and she admired Jibril's tremendous talent in silent magic. [26] [27]

She met Claude Yui when he was a child; they had a sort of mentor-student relationship. [28] In the present, Laila often gets frustrated when Claude lacks off with his duties and does not hesitate to reprimand the priest.

Agwen initially appears as a cheerful and independent woman, who might have tendencies to boss around other people. History

Agwen is the only child of the half-dragon Kasak Rajof and a pure-blood fighter, Meiwen Hael. Her father would usually wear special earrings which suppressed his dragon indifference. She never got to meet her grandmother, Ian Rajof, as the woman was already dead when Kasak finally chose to introduce his wife and daughter to his parents. She, however, got to meet her grandfather, Taksaka, at the occasion.[7]

When Agwen was little, Shess would visit Kasak's family. She would play with Shess and give hats to him.[4] Her mother got injured at some point and had to retire as a fighter. Agwen found herself a fiancée who she was to marry.[8]

Taksaka would visit Kasak's family in the human realm. He was present during the fighters championship in D995 where he wore the earrings rather than Kasak.[9] An incident leading to the death of Airi Yui has been hinted to have happened on that day.[10]

During the Cataclysm of N0, under the influence of massive emotional resonance, Kasak went berserk and killed Agwen's mother, best friend, and fiancée.[6] He was said to have done massive damage in Rindhallow.[11] Agwen managed to defend herself and survive somehow. She was able to emotionally recover from the event, but still becomes upset with her father's indifference when he is not wearing the earrings.

Sometime after N5, Agwen was one of several priest candidates who left Atera after Brilith Ruin's flawless barrier made their jobs unnecessary.[12]

Agwen later became a professor at Eloth University, and Asha Rahiro was one of her students.[13] She was known for being very strict.[1] Agwen is also an advocate for half rights and she has been buying out shards of Yaksha's bones and destroying them so that half hunters cannot use them.[5]

The Finite
The Blog Version of the finite and the Naver Best Challenge version have slightly different content.

Ian was born in a village of worshippers of the Vritra sura, and grew up there, till a sura proclaiming to be the dragon Taksaka demanded Ian as sacrifice from the villagers. However, her parents hid her away and the dragon destroyed the village. Ian barely survived the annihilation.

She wandered from city to city, but having been raised in the faith of the sura, and therefore regarded as heretic, everyone turned their back on her, until the Mistyshore authorities accepted to take her in on the condition that she publicly renounced her faith in front of the temple of Preservation. She made the oath to take down the Dragon of Destruction Taksaka and to become a great magician. Unfortunately, she later discovered that her double-Nil attribute resulted a high magic failure rate, so no magic school accepted her application.

Eight years passed. She started working in the Mistyshore Magic Shopping Mall to make a living.

One day, while complaining for being rejected again by a magic school, she saw someone drowning in the sea, and didn't hesitate to jump to save that person. But he wasn't drowning, and instead was simply floating in the water, and after Ian realized she was outside of the barrier's protection, the boy helped her coming back to the shore. Unknown to her, the boy was Taksaka himself. And Ian, pressed by him, revealed that her goal was to kill that same Taksaka who destroyed her village. The sura asked for more information, but dismissed Ian's suspicions saying that no sura would impersonate another one. Despite his vague responses, Ian concluded that he was a half, and asked for his name, to which he replied "Tak" (a nickname only three people were allowed to use - Vasuki, Visnu, and Airavata). That being said, Ian went back into the city, leaving Tak outside, since he could not enter without a sponsor.

The following day Ian was coaxed into delivering warm milk to "a guy sleeping on a rock" outside of the city by a disguised Visnu. To her surprise, the guy was none other than the Half she met the day before. When she wanted to leave after the delivery, Tak tried to hold her back, accidentally breaking her arm in the process. She was scared and cried when he kept her from running away. Tak apologized to her only after putting on the earrings and brought her to the checkpoint as fast as possible so that she would get treatment.

She has blond hair and blue eyes, and prefers to wear red armor. She has red markings around the outer corners of her eyes, which are often mistaken for make-up, but are in fact the few remaining signs of her sura heritage.

In season 3, Teo wears her hair short and loose. She is usually seen wearing casual and comfortable clothing.

Personality
She tends to be very frank and confident in her manner, speaking her mind plainly. She is very friendly towards halfs, gaining her A+ magic license just to increase the numbers of halfs she can sponsor. Despite this, she has reached her half-sponsorship limit, though she still has room for humans. Her hobby is collecting rare items, especially weapons.

She is rivals with Airi Yui. When Airi is mentioned she says, "Don't talk about HER in front of me!"

Although the Temple of Chaos gets fewer and fewer visitors each year, Teo still takes care to decorate the temple carefully. Since the Chaos barrier does not require her to actively maintain it, she only stays within the barrier's boundaries, which is her duty as the Priest of Chaos.

Skills and Abilities
Despite having an A+ magician rank, she has terrible magic abilities, some say worse than some Academy students, and she herself claims she took the magic exam with just her physical abilities and transcendental skills. However, she seems to be proficient with hoti kubera; during her walk in the snow with Gandharva to the Earth barrier checkpoint, she frets that she needs to save up her uses of hoti kubera,[1] and she uses the spell on her entire body when she faces Sagara.[2]

Due to her triple-Nil (formerly Chaos) attributes, she is able to use Chaos silent magic, which in theory should no longer exist. She uses Transcendental Resistance against Pingara's electric transcendental, which reduces damage from magic and transcendentals by 99% for triple-Nils.

She is a quarter and a genius fighter with high physical abilities and weapon techniques, supplemented by her transcendental skills, becoming President of the Kalibloom Fighters Guild at a relatively young age. She was the winner of the N7 Fighter Championship, and runner-up in the N11, N15, and N19 Championships.


Being Priest of Chaos does not require any skill or ability on her part, as the barrier activates when anyone with triple-Nil attributes walks into range. Other barriers require a priest to use energy directly to get the barriers to work. Whether or not this takes any energy from her when the barrier is active is unknown.
