Plot
History
Enan's mother used to be one of the Blood Knights, an order of fiendish magic users who served the king of humans (also known as the 16th daksha). When fiendish magic became dangerous, the king ordered that his knights quit using it. Every knight disobeyed, and they were executed. Since then, he has decided to get revenge on the king for his actions, along with his companion.

Season 1
Enan is mentioned to Kubera Leez as the first owner of the Golden Knight. He was a fighter who became a priest when he received the bracelet.(4)

Season 3
Chapter 53: Ananta
Enan comes across Maruna on the border of Taitalika. He warns him to be careful if he is a superior sura for the gods who are present do not take well to suras at the time. Maruna finds the man's behavior strange and chooses to inconspiciously follow. Along with his companion, Enan discusses that he will be taking part in some tournament. He has no innate divine affinity but he is confident that he can win because he has the Golden Knight bracelet.[2] Enan then drags Maruna into a restaurant within the cities. Maruna is first annoyed to see the menu but gets interested when Enan orders a snowflake apple for himself. Maruna takes it from under Enan's nose and is surprised to find out that it is delicious.

Within the city, rumors spread that the human king has collected all five Vajras. Enan asks Maruna where he plans to go. Maruna notices that the Golden Knight was given specifically to Enan and surmises that staying with Enan might give him an opportunity to meet god Kubera.[3] Enan Reimia registers for the competition in the city. He explains that he is a pureblood fighter who mainly uses Kubera magic. His friend later chastises him for lying, as Enan is able to use magic only through virtue of the Golden Knight bracelet, since his divine affinity is practically nonexistant. The winner of the competition will become a member of the royal family. They ask Maruna if he would perhaps like to participate as well.

Maruna and Enan are at a stadium where they observe the first matches of the tournament. It is announced that matches between halfs and other humans will be held separately and will intersect only in the final round. Enan states that the king and gods are only interested in the matches of purebloods and quarters. A magician in a match uses Sanyoga Menaka, a spell that lets them nullify damage. Biting back his pride, Maruna asks Enan to explain more about the fiendish magic he might encounter. Enan explains them to him.

Suddenly, an announcement declares that only purebloods will be allowed to compete and all other participents will be sent back, they will get their admission fee refunded. Rumor has it that the king dreamt that someone with sura blood will bring about disaster. Enan has trouble convincing the organizers that he is a pureblood but they are finally convinced when they register his divine affinity of 2250 which would be impossible for a quarter. Maruna recalls that Enan actually has 0 divine affinity and this higher number is caused by the golden knight.[5]

It is soon time for Enan's performance. Enan kills his opponent quickly to progress as soon as possible. Enan beats another opponent and raises to the top 16.[6]He finally progresses into the semifinals. A group of participating magicians come chat with Enan in good nature. One of them is Artram, a revolutionary Creation magician and priest of Creation. An attendant comes for Enan with word that the king wishes to speak with him privately. People speculate that perhaps Enan is to be appointed as Priest of Earth.

Enan meets with the king, Maruna and the girl are observing in hiding. The king reveals that he has recognized Enan as a descendent of the knights who survived his slaughters. And then, to the surprise of all, he falls to his knees and apologizes. He feels that he has committed a great evil and has admiration for the knights who would rather burn than break their contracts with nastikas. He must have accumulated many sins due to the resulting grudges. Enan feels the need to clarify that the knights chose not to break their contracts because they knew the nastikas would then come for revenge and likely threaten the king. As things stand, the king misunderstood their reasons. The king is surprised by this interpretation and claims that a god who read the knights' minds told him something that would contradict it. At that moment, Indra shows up, putting an end to the conversation.[7]

Indra asserts that the human king was right to punish the knights. The king grasps the vajra and his entire attitude changes, now expressing scorn for Enan. Enan and the king fight, destroying the palace all around them. The king has the upper hand, and Enan appears defeated. The king makes an arrogant speech over his body. He then calls out Kubera, making it obvious the second god did not go unnoticed. Yet Kubera is nowhere to be seen. Indra feels that Kubera had been scheming towards this moment. Suddenly, Enan regenerates due to his bracelet and he attacks the king with a Sanyoga Ananta spell. The king is defeated.[8]

The human king awakens surrounding by his attendants. Enan is tied up before him. The king immediately requests that he is released. The king explains that he did not act of his will and does not remember his actions. His only desire was to apologize. Once again, he falls to his knees and he offers to accept Enan into the royal family and make him Priest of Earth. A hooded man steps beside Enan. It is Ananta, claiming that he came to retaliate since he did not like the request of the contractor who used his magic just then.

The people around speculate about Ananta's identity. Enan attempts to pretend that Ananta is a merchant to whom he owns money. To his surprise, Ananta plays along. However, Ananta asks for Enan to remove the Golden Knight bracelet. When Enan expresses worry at the people watching, Ananta stops time. Then, time continues to flow again.

The people in the room all bow before god Kubera who is still standing beside Enan. Kubera asks the king to reveal whether Indra was the one who ordered the murder of the knight order. if The king cant reveal it, then he will have pay for the crimes of murder along with blasphemy for blaming a god. however, if he confirms it was Indra, then Kubera will call upon Indra and check the truth with him.[10] The king denies Indra's involvement in his actions and claims to have received his oracles from planetary gods. Kubera finds this hard to believe for his insight implies that someone of equal or higher rank than himself must have been involved. Enan's friend interrupts declaring that she knows the true mastermind. She says it is a being whose name they do not know and are unsure if they are a god, theirs is the temple of time. Kubera asks her to go to the temple with him and Enan insists on tagging along.

Kubera, Enan, and Enan's friend reach the temple of time, Maruna follows them from hiding. Kubera deduces that the girl could not possibly have known the truth on her own, so he pressures her until she admits that she heard nothing and only knew what was said from Kinnara. Kubera figures that she must have been afraid of Kinnara's retaliation and he sets out to investigate the nastika. The girl worries about Kinnara's well-being since she considers Kinnara a person who reached out to her when she was in need. Enan suggests that the girl alerts Kinnara about Kubera by using her magic.[11]

Enan leaves the cavern and encounters Maruna outside. Kubera is already gone. Enan explains that his friend means to draw out Kinnara and that she needs to be alone. Maruna has a bad opinion on nastikas and disapproves of bringing one over. Enan attempts to argue. Enan also explains that his desire for revenge isn't as great as the girl's. She was merely the sister of a merchant who traded with the Knights and thus it was unfair that she got enslaved. She saw Kinnara as a savior. A light shoots up from the cavern, leaving a crater behind. Maruna and Enan see Kinnara - now Airavata (her form changed to what we know from the current timeline) standing over the girl with her spear.

Enan rushes forward without thinking and casts Sanvega Ananta.[12] Enan attacks Airavata and gets crashed into a wall. Airavata decides not to kill him in respect of the girl. When he seems unable to accept the decision, she suggests altering his memory. Enan casts Sanyoga Ananta and Airavata freezes in time. He rushes to pull out the spear from his friend. Maruna helps him. Airavata unfreezes and expresses anger at the two. Before she can harm them, Kubera picks up the spear and faces off Airavata. Enan picks up his friend and takes her to safety. Yama arrives at the scene and proclaims that Airavata was supposed to live with the consequences of bearing two names and should prepare for the afterlife.[13]

Maruna carries Enan and his friend, taking on sura form to get the humans away quickly. Enan is calling out to his comatose friend with the name Kinnara. Maruna wonders if that was the girl's name from the start. Maruna evades a ball of light that nearly hits him. When he looks back to find out who is attacking him, he sees his father, Garuda.[14] He worries that his father might misunderstand if he sees that Maruna is carrying humans so he forces Enan and the girl to get off.[15]

Enan is later found unconscious, with his friend Kinnara looming over his injured body.

However, Ran has also said that Lutz is not as nice of a guy as he appears.[3] Lutz rallies other high-ranking wizards to support Asha should the issue of her criminal cases become a problem, and argues that the number of lives she saves and can still save is worth the sacrifice of a few.[4] He also grudgingly agrees with Claude that Leez should be sacrificed in order to keep Yuta on the side of humanity, otherwise the humans will lose the war.

Skills and Abilities

Being a triple-Brahma magician, he is strong with both hoti brahma and bhavati brahma. He has also been shown to cast fusion spells, such as hoti indra bhavati brahma[6] and hoti brahma bhavati brahma.[7] Lutz is skilled at using creation silent magic, imaginary correction.[8]

Lutz's magician ranking is 23rd, which belies his actual capabilities due to him not fully applying himself during his magic exam.[9] Tilda states that Lutz could easily have gotten an AA rank if he had wanted to.[10] He mentioned having more than enough vigor for his barrier to Siera,[11] which is rather unusual, since even the quarter Laila gets overly tired. He also has enough vigor to fire the Neutral Bow,[12] possibly due to being the grandson of a nastika King.

Lutz placed 2nd in the N7 Fighter Championships. He then did not compete for many years until N19 where he ranked 3rd.

Notes
His Yaksha heritage is confirmed through the Kubera side-novel, the finite. Unbeknownst to him, his grandmother is the current Yaksha King, succeeding both Shuri, who had disappeared, and Yaksha, who is deceased.
Lutz's side business, the Creation brand Artram, is the biggest competitor to Riche Seiran's company, the Creation brand Brimo.[13]
The reason he deliberately obtained a lower score than he was capable of in his magic exam was to stay with his brother, Ran Sairofe, instead of becoming the Priest of Creation, which he ended up becoming anyway.[9]
Fun fact: Lutz, the most handsome human male character,[2] and Saha On, the human male character with the greatest feminine beauty, are co-priests of Eloth.
He gets many neckties as presents. He tries to wear them all, no matter how weird they are. [11]

Lutz Sairofe is the oldest child of Hana Lehn and Tan Sairofe and the older brother of Ran Sairofe.

Riche appears as a young woman with light skin tone. She has pale, blueish-green hair like her sister Ruche, and similar pink eyes. In contrast to her sister, she wears glasses and her hairstyle is slightly different and more disheveled. She often changes her clothes, but she is always been seen in a dress, sometimes with a wide-collar jacket or a cape.

Personality
The writing on her fan reads "Mine is mine. Yours is mine," which suggests she is possessive and greedy. When Teo Rakan mentioned how some people will acquire rare items by any means necessary, Riche's image accompanied her words. It seems Teo and Riche had a kind of rivalry to grab rare items first, although Teo acquired hers legally.

Unlike her twin sister, she isn't a magician because her divine affinity is too low.

Notes
The greatest competitor to Riche's company, the Creation Brand 'Brimo', is the Creation Brand 'Artram' run by Lutz Sairofe.

Plot
History
In the year D995, when Mirha was 9 years old, Mirha's father Urha left planet Carte for Willarv to become their Priest of Sky.[6] In the year N0, Mirha was 14 years old (7 in appearance) when her mother was affected by emotional resonance in the Cataclysm and was killed. Mirha inherited all of her mother's remaining property as a result. Since her father was away, she effectively became an orphan, and was taken care of by one of her mother's good friends—Asha Rahiro's mother. Mirha and Asha were raised like sisters, but Asha only tolerated the more socially-adept Mirha. When it was time to enroll in the Eos Magic Academy, Mirha learned that her divine affinity was 1830, higher than that of the Priest of Wind on Carte, which was 1500.[9] In the year N5, when Carte was under attack, Mirha continued to want to be friends with Asha, but her wish was one-sided since Asha had no interest in friendship.[1]

She murdered the previous Priest of Light during the Cataclysm in the year N0,[3] likely due to the massive occurrence of emotional resonance.[4] She was quickly killed by the combined attacks of the priest candidates, and the Sword returned itself to its resting place at the Temple of Chaos where Kali originally dropped it.[5][6]

Appearance
Hana appears to be a woman with a light-brown skin tone. She has long light gray hair, which she puts up in pigtails (similar to her son Ran). So far her eye color has not been revealed, since her long bangs usually cover up her eyes. Her sura attributes are a long light gray tail, and light gray fur on the lower part of her arms.

She usually wears clothes typical for exercise or combat, often a simply colored tight tank top (in black or white), and long or short sport trousers in darker colors (gray or gray-blue).

Her preferred weapon of choice seem to be a pair of identical swords which she carries around with her in a scabbard adjusted at the belt.

Notes
In Asian martial arts, a choice of double weapons or double swords is often traditionally preferred by female fighters. It is possible that this is the reason Currygom gave Hana two swords to carry at all times.

In a flashback to D997, Hana is seen gifting gloves advertised by a famous fighter to her son Ran as an apology for not being there for his birthday. Thankful for his gift, Ran shows his mom his fighting skills ahead of the Youth Martial Arts Competition. Hana claps enthusiastically and encourages Ran to hit a rock. The atmosphere ends prematurely however when her husband joins them. Protective of her son, Hana yells at Tan to shut up when he dampens the mood by calling the competition childish and comparing Ran to Lutz. When Ran talks back at his father and runs away, Hana tells Tan to leave their son be as Lutz, who Ran considers not only as his older brother, but also a friend, teacher, and even parent, is leaving him for Eloth.

(2) In the year D999, Ran makes it clear to his uncle that he's only reluctantly attending Mistyshore Public Academy of Magic to appease his mom and brother.

(3) In the year D1000/N0, Hana asks her son how he's liking the Academy. When Ran releases all his frustration and dislike for the school and the people there, Hana points out the he never skipped a single day. Hana suddenly brings up Rana and how she's pretty. Ran perks up before realizing how his mother would know that; Hana exclaims of a meat buffet as a distraction. Unwilling to drop the matter, Ran speculates it was his uncle who told her and reaffirms that him and Rana are nothing but friends. Hana clarifies she doesn't feel the same way for the matter as Huan does. How could she when she, a half, married Tan, a pure-blooded human. Hana mentions of an even more contrasting relationship: Her parents who consisted of a quarter magician and a nastika. Assuming that their conversation was a way of his mother giving him his blessing, Ran announces he'll ask Rana out, but Hana interrupt he can't. She explains to Ran the problem with relationships between a long-living being and a human start with their differing notions of time and how it seeps into how long an individual can love a single person. All Hana wants is for her son to be in love with someone who has a longer lifespan than him, that way he will never feel the heartbreak of knowing he is no longer loved by the one he loves the most. Hesitating, Ran asks his mother if dad said anything to her. He noticed them being distant since she returned to Mistyshore. Hana ignores Ran's worries to concentrate on the meat buffet. She tells him not to worry and that what ever happens with his dad, she will always love him and will never leave him behind.

It's later revealed Hana was killed in year N0 during the Cataclysm when she turned insane and brutally attacked her own family due to emotional resonance. In a flashback to that moment, she is seen looming over a crying little Ran.

Tilda has been shown to take her job seriously, and watches closely over her boss, Saha.

She has excellent memory, but is not very smart in any other way.[1]

Notes

It is not yet known why Ran, who has a great fear of halfs, is completely relaxed around Tilda.[2]
It is not yet known why Yuta wants to eat her.[2]

Kasak Rajof is a half-blood human of Vritra heritage, and the only living dragon on Planet Willarv. He also appears in the finite.

Appearance
In his human form, Kasak appears as a man with grayish skin tone. He has long dark grey hair, black eyebrows and dark red eyes. He has four blackish medium-length and upwards-curved horns on either side of his head. He has fangs and claws. In his arms, the dark grayish skin extends above his elbows and his arms have large spikes on the back side, below his elbow. The top side oh his hands and fingers are covered with a pinkish-red pattern, that ends in protruding pinkish-red claws at the tips of his fingers. He is wearing grey shoes and light grey trousers, that are held up by a brown waist-strap. On his upper-body he wears a darker-grayish shirt and a black vest with a large neck-piece on top of it.

When he wears Vishnu's earrings, he appears almost completely human, differing only by his grayish skin tone. He differs from his human form by having no horns, having normal teeth and having normal hands with red wristbands.

In his sura form, Kasak appears as a large dragon. He has dark skin, red eyes, a long pinkish mane, two arms and legs, wings and one very long sharp-scaled tail. Kasak has two brownish horns of medium length at the back of his head. His wings appear to consist of grey skin and a black non-solid matter in the end that disperses into the air as he flies. His dark legs have bony red knee-caps, that elongate as shin-guards to his toes, forming large protruding claws. Kasak's arms have sharp scales around his elbow area, and a pinkish-red pointy scale on top, that elongates to his fingers and forms large protruding claws.

Personality
With the earrings on, Kasak appears to have a laid-back and playful personality. He is on several occasions shown to play around with Yuta. Like normal people, he has a wide range of emotions. He was capable of falling in love and lead a normal life among humans.

As a half-dragon, his feelings are numbed, but not to the extent of Vritra nastikas. In comparison with his father, Agni even described him as talkative. Kasak is capable of feeling anger, sadness, concern, guilt and fear without the earrings. His problem is that he doesn't express them with the intensity that a normal person would, making him appear cold and distant. He has a reckless side to his personality, being quite happy when exercising his physical abilities and transcendental skills and showed no fear when facing multiple rakshasa-rank suras.

Agwen is afraid of him without the earrings, something that Kasak is aware of and bothers him. He understands her reaction and tries not to force her to spend time with him when he doesn't have the earrings. He lets his daughter order him around when using the earrings as a sort of redemption for killing his wife and hurting Agwen with his words.

He is scared of his father because of how Taksaka treated him when he was a child. Because his mother lost 80 years of her life to have Kasak, his father hated him at first and came close to kill him almost daily. They weren't very close and Kasak resented that his father abandoned him. In time, their relationship improved and Tak visited him and Agwen until N0.

His mother Ian loved Kasak deeply and never regretted losing 80 years of her life for him. She was a devoted mother and tried her best to make her son happy. Kasak was very possessive of Ian, which sparked some friction with Tak. Ian protected her son from her husband's anger and made Taksaka promise to take care of Kasak when she died.

Plot

History

Kasak was born in D883. He had a strained relationship with his father from the beginning, since he had cost his mother 80 years of her life and didn't resemble her at all.

Once, when Kasak was 10 years, he hurt his mother using his Breath because he was jealous she didn't spend all the time with him. Vishnu warned Taksaka and Nard about what had happened and they arrived in time to save Ian. As a punishment, Tak hurt Kasak. When Ian found out, she became angry and made the dragon promise he would never hurt their son again.

He is once held by Vishnu, whom he humorously shoots with his Destructive Breath, with his mother and father nearby. Due his father's friendships, the Half dragon met and befriended some sura as a child, like Shess and Kalavinka. At one point, a young Kasak is shown talking to a 3rd stage Kalavinka. He asks her if she lives with Vishnu because she does not have a family and offers to give Kalavinka his dad. She explains she has a family, but they have to stay apart for a while due to the Power of the Name. The young Half asks what that is and Kalavinka says she can't tell him about it. She requests that he doesn't share information on her whereabouts with anyone. Kasak promises her he won't.

As Kasak grew up, Ian noted he needed a Half identification, so the three of them went to Mistyshore to get it. Both of his parents were identified in the checkpoint and he obtained his ID card. On Ian's whim, they pay a visit to the restaurant where she used to work. Kasak and Tak had a brief conversation regarding their relationship and the dragon admitted he didn't hate his son anymore, but says he would have loved a daughter that resembled Ian. Kasak was deeply wounded by his words, since there was nothing he could do to have his father's love.

In the autumn of D951, Kasak decided to participate in the Fighter Championship. Taksaka reminded him that he wasn't allowed to kill opponents and asked if he was sure he could control or restrain himself. Ian proposed that Tak lend the earrings to Kasak for the championship. There he met his future wife, Meiwen Hael. She was his sponsor for entering Kalibloom. He was looking for a man to sponsor him in order not to bother a woman, but because of her short hair, Kasak confused her with a man.

When the Half dragon returned, he asked if he could keep the earrings for a little longer, because he didn't want to scare his girlfriend. Ian supported this idea, mentioning she didn't mind living with Taksaka without the earrings. Their son left for 10 years with the earrings, after hearing from Vishnu that his mother would die in D963.

Kasak married Meiwen and had Agwen. In D961, he returned home in order to show his daughter to his parents. No one answered the door, but it was open. The house was clean and in order, however, no food or drinks were in sight. Kasak found their parents in the second floor, only to realize his mother had died a while ago. He gave the earrings back to his father, so that he was able to cry for his wife. They scattered her ashes in a nearby river. Taksaka returned to the sura realm afterwards, but continued to visit Kasak and Agwen until N0.

During the N0 Cataclysm, Kasak was caught in emotional resonance. He killed his wife, Agwen's best friend, and her lover. Agwen herself barely managed to survive. She was very shocked that her father would be so calm after what he had done. He explained he didn't love Meiwen or her without the earrings, which hurt Agwen. Despite growing afraid of her father, she forgave him and sponsored him.

 In D875, Manasvin visits Vasuki at Taksaka's nest to give him a letter from Riagara. He learns that Taksaka is off playing house in the human realm at the moment.

Spin-off Episode 18 - In My Delusion (Vol 1)
We learn that Ananta was the original god of this universe, known at the time as the Great Snake. He had a female companion named Manasa. She had the ability to manipulate time, which she used to do good for those who needed help in the universe. During this time beings calling themselves the Primeval Gods appeared and clashed with Ananta and Manasa. Over time, the use of the time ability tore away at her soul and she became corrupted. The Primaeval Gods fought against her and slew her. Ananta in his grief collected the shards of her broken soul and asked the god Resurrection that she be brought back to life. He replied that he could use parts of her shattered soul to place into another living being, but she may not reassemble the Manasa he once knew. Resurrection attempted to bring her back but ran into trouble making the broken pieces work. He ended up taking a piece of her broken name, combining it with another name, and created a new male being known as Manasvin. The remaining parts of her soul was placed in a being with a totally different name, Sagara. Manasvin evoked a similar vibe in personality to Manasa and inherited the power of her broken name. Sagara received the looks that Manasa had but her power and personality was far different than the original. Distraught with the outcome, Ananta used his own time ability to try and change what happened. However, no matter how far back he went, even until the beginning of time, Manasa no longer existed and was replaced by a combination of Manasvin and Sagara instead.

Human Form
Saan takes the appearance of a young man in his 20s.[1] He has short light purple hair with thick bangs, with long strands framing his face. He wears rather formal attire, with a grey dress shirt along with a black sweater on top of it. His pants match his sweater while his shoes are darker.

His sura trait takes the form of his wings, they take a similar appearance to single feathers, being comprised of a long grey shaft with blue and purple barbs at their ends. He is capable of having four wings, but can remove the top two when needed.

Personality
Saan appeared loyal to his king Ananta, attempting to rally other clans to go to his rescue. Later, so enraged at Ananta's death, Saan charged at the gods out of rage.[2]

Plot
Chapter 20: Grudge

In D500, Saan joins up with Manasvin and Sagara at the Ananta stronghold. He warns Manasvin that they cannot count on any support from the other clans to save Ananta. He states that the Asuras are busy fighting the Yakshas and Garudas, and that the Kinnaras are having internal conflict due to issues regarding 'The Power of the Name'. Saan comments that he was relieved at the arrival of Taksaka, but is disappointed that the Vritra is just watching the fight. In the end, the only options they have left is to either abandon Ananta or risk many lives trying to save him, stating that with Vasuki already gone ahead, Manasvin is the one that has to make the decision for their clan.

Sagara questions why the Gandharva clan isn't helping them, with Saan recalling his meeting with them. When he approached them on the planet Carte, he was received by Gandharva, Makara, Urvasi, and Menaka. At first, the Gandharvas offered their help until Menaka voiced her disagreement as she did not want their clan to fight. Saan attempted to explain more, but Gandharva had no interest in hearing anything but what Menaka had to say. Manasvin makes the decision to go attempt to save Ananta, with Saan accompanying him.

Appearance
In her human form, Riagara appears as a woman with light-grayish skin tone. She has long orange-brownish hair, very thin grayish eyebrows and red eyes with vertically-elongated (snake-like) pupils. She wears a high-soled full bodysuit, that has a thick brown neck-guard. The suit is colored brown at the outer sides of arms, body and legs and dark brown on the insides, and has a brown zipper-like line going down from the neck-guard at the front.

As a child, her appearance slightly differed from her adult form. She had much shorter hair that was tied in back. She appeared to be wearing a dark brown sports-shirt. Her hands were covered with a brown material which seemed to be a substitute for her skin, starting from the arms-down.

In her sura form, Riagara appears as a red and brown-scaled snake. She has long orange-brownish hair, red eyes, dark brown face area, and a large brown scale with a dark brown spiky outer layer covering her head.

Personality
Riagara appears to have a quiet personality. She keeps her calm when troubled by attempts to distract or taunt her. She is quick to act and independent in her decisions when the time calls for it, which is shown on many occasions. Riagara appears to be closer to Sagara than Pingara, and is also capable of manipulating others to get her way.

She is also one of the Ananta rakshasas who protect Sagara, since the other clan members (except for Vasuki) do not accept her as their king, and her role is to protect Sagara when Vasuki is not around. Her loyalty to Sagara is unwavering and she never questions her orders, because "Sagara is always right". Riagara can get upset if someone doubts or criticizes Sagara.

It is confirmed that Riagara is the daughter of Vasuki and Sagara in Episode 3-126, where Pingara claims that since Sagara would have no affection left for her former lover, Vasuki, their child, Riagara, would also be no better than a stranger to her.
In her third stage, Riagara has had many lovers, allegedly more than you could count on the fingers of both hands. However, she has not dated anyone since developing to fourth stage.[4]
Plot
History

Riagara is the daughter of Sagara and Vasuki.[5] As a child, she spent much of her time living in Taksaka's nest in the sura realm along with Vasuki, who raised her, and Taksaka, who taught her how to fight.[6][2] She would visit her siblings and get excited when her mother would drop by.[6] Despite mostly having lived in the sura realm, Riagara visited the human realm several times, either with Vasuki[7] or with her siblings, concluding that it is not an enviable place to live in.

Pingara

Pingara is a rakshasa of the Ananta clan. He is part of Sagara's core group and is currently in the human realm.
Note: Pingara's gender is unknown and the author Currygom has stated that it will never be revealed in the webtoon.[1] For this reason, this article uses the pronouns he/him/his to refer to Pingara.

Appearance
In human form, Pingara has a light-grayish skin tone and a tail. He has long bluish-gray hair and red eyes with vertically elongated pupils. He wears a blueish-black overcoat with a lighter lining on the topside, that covers his entire body. Pingara seems to keep his hair inside the coat.

In his sura form, he appears as a large snake with grayish scaled belly and smooth bluish-black top side. He has red eyes and three hornlike extensions on his head, two on the sides, and one on the top. The side-extensions are curved front and downwards, and the top extension protrudes in the front and is curved backwards. His face is grayish and has a blueish-gray pattern that starts from his eyes and extends to and one large part covers his horns.

Personality
Pingara appears to have a serious and quiet personality. He is rarely seen talking to anybody but Riagara and Sagara. Despite this, he has shown not to be as blind as Riagara when it comes to Sagara. [2]

When Pingara was younger, his personality was very different. He was easily excited and quick to show awe and emotions of all kind. It has been implied that some trauma led to his change in personality.

This skill can be used in sura or human form. Upon using another transcendental skill, the cloaking wears off first before the other transcendental begins.

	Electric Field

Effect: It releases a strong electrical current along a constant radius around the user.
This transcendental has no effect on targets in the air.

Spectator

Effect: It turns the user physically intangible, preventing damage even when the hiding spot is hit.
The user must stay motionless in order to maintain the effect. The user will be momentarily paralyzed upon release from the skill.

This skill can only use shadows cast by sunlight, so due to weather conditions and the time of day, this skill can become useless.

This skill can be used in sura and human form. It is impossible to target someone directly with this skill.

He is an expert at hiding.[4]

The fact that Pingara is the child of Sagara was confirmed in Episode 3-126.

Plot

History
Pingara is the child of Sagara and Manasvin and he would have been born at most 600 years ago.[5][6] He was raised mostly in the sura realm, having visited the human realm only briefly taking bad memories from the experience.[3] He would often get to meet up with his siblings, even if they lived apart. When he was little, Maruna tried to hunt him, which has considerably traumatized Pingara.[4]

Appearance
In her human form, Cloche appears as a young girl with slightly pale skin tone. She has long brown hair that she ties into two spiraling side-ponytails with gold-colored ribbons. She has thin brown eyebrows, red eyes with vertically elongated pupils and a black line under the lateral part of both of her eyes. Her outfit is composed of a long, gold-colored dress that appears spiky above the chest, a pair of matching gloves that reach midway between her shoulder and elbow and are spiky at the ends. She also wears a piece of lighter-gold cloth wrapped around her waist and tied in back.

Currygom describes her as looking more youthful than her fellow 4th-stage rakshasas Riagara and Pingara.

In her sura form, she appears as a large, dark gold, snake-like creature. She has large lighter gold feathered wings, feathered patches along her body and feathered ears (that resemble Maruna's in his human form). Cloche has red eyes, a small red forked tongue and two sharp teeth on each jaw. She has two thin brown lines, that start from below her eyes, make a zig-zag behind her eyes, pass below her ears and elongate beyond the base of her wings.

Personality
Cloche can be somewhat emotional, being susceptible to taunts and quick to anger. she appears to be true to her words and discipline, going on with the plan and continuing to destroy the city, even after several potentially lethal failed attempts at doing so (although she shows signs of lacking confidence when initiating her second attack). Her lack of battle-sense and experience is apparent when she is rather easily felled by only a few magicians.[2] She cares about Clophe and protects him in his weakened state, refusing to leave him.[3]

Notes
Cloche and Clophe have rakshasa/nastika parents, which makes them weaker than normal rakshasas born between two nastika parents.[7] Their mother was a rakshasa and their father was a nastika.[8]
Cloche specializes in transcendentals, while Clophe specializes in hand-to-hand combat. Out of Sagara's group, she has the strongest transcendentals, but their long delays make it easy for magicians to seal them with bhavati asvins.[7]
"Cloche" means both "bell" in French and a woman's hat with a bell-shaped crown in English; however, the character name (kloh-cheh) and the English/French words (klohsh) are pronounced differently.

Clophe and Cloche are twins, though Clophe was born first. They are older than Pingara.[8]
Plot
History
Cloche is the child of a nastika father and a rakshasa mother. She was mostly raised in the human realm under the care of her older upani half-brother Chloe, and with the presence of her mother. Despite having developed to fourth stage long before D875, she was not considering having children of her own because she felt it was time-consuming enough to care for her older twin brother who was still in second stage until that year. She would meet up with Pingara and Riagara and brag about the beauty of her home.[8]

Appearance
In his human form, Clophe appears as a boy in his mid-teens with slightly pale skin tone. He has brown hair of medium length, thin brown eyebrows, and red eyes with vertically elongated pupils. He has black lines under his eyes. He also has a tail that is not very obvious. His outfit is composed of dark-purplish trousers and a blue shirt with a messy neck-piece and very long sleeves which cover his clawed hands. He wears a piece of purplish cloth around his waist and is usually barefoot. He was however seen wearing very dark blue shoes at one point.

In his sura form, Clophe looks like a large snake-like creature. He has a lighter-blue smooth belly-side and a darker-blue spiky back-side. He has red eyes, long sharp ears that are lighter-blue in front and darker-blue on the backside, and two darker-blue spiky arms with claws.

Personality
His personality seems to depend on whether or not he is in sura form. In his human form, he appears weak and timid. In his sura form, he shows more confidence. Unlike the other suras, he seems less interested in causing destruction and havoc, even in Atera. He does execute his power when protecting those he cares for and retaliates when attacked. Clophe seems to have a close relationship with his sister Cloche, saving her from the magicians. An important part of his personality is his curiosity; once Airi Yui catches his attention, he starts chasing her around, disregarding Cloche's pleas for help since he had never seen a human take on a rakshasa on her own.

Clophe refuses to speak in the presence of suras other than Cloche, and will only talk to her when they are alone.[1][2] Clophe dislikes fighting and this makes it difficult for him to train to develop.[3]

Skills and Abilities
Unlike his sister, who primarily uses transcendental skills in combat, Clophe focuses on physical combat and destruction. He has only been shown using one of his transcendentals, Frosty Field, so far.[4]

Notes
Clophe is Cloche's older twin-brother, but thanks to his slower development he is mistaken for the younger of the two siblings.[5] They are older than Pingara.[3]
His key for development is most likely either survival instinct or the death of a sibling.[3]
He never talks except when he and Cloche are alone. The only exception to this is when he talks to Airi Yui while she tries to fight against him, although she is unable to hear him. He only ever spoke to Riagara once.[3]
One of his and Cloche's parents is a rakshasa, so the siblings are weaker than normal rakshasas born between two nastikas parents.[5] Their mother was a rakshasa and their father was a nastika.

Plot
History
Clophe is the child of a nastika father and a rakshasa mother. He was mostly raised in the human realm under the care of his older upani half-brother Chloe, and with the presence of their mother. Clophe is an extremely slow developer and was still at 2nd stage in D875 when his twin sister Cloche was already at 4th stage and Pingara, who is younger than the both of them, was at third stage. Clophe developed to third stage under further unspecified circumstances when the galaxy he and his sister lived in was destroyed.[3]

During the early universe, he orchestrated fights with Yaksha to showcase that Yaksha's power in an era of correcting mistakes.[2] Asura also ensured to maintain a civil relationship with Chandra, as he is the God of Darkness, which is his clan's attribute.[3]

As the king of the Asura clan, Asura is the strongest sura in his clan. Currently, he is the second strongest sura in the entire sura realm behind Vritra. Personality
His personality is altogether described as rotten. He is quickly to mock other people and taunt them, which proves a mistake of his when he tries this with Taksaka. Ravana is arrogant, since he considers himself to be above others due his strength and influence with Asura. In the finite, he even hosts a party from Asura's seat and leaves a mess behind after leaving. As the second ranked nastika in the Asura clan, Ravana is incredibly powerful. Famous for her regeneration skills, she is categorized as the un-killable one along with Gandharva.[4] Ravana's sura form takes the shape of a bee swarm, allowing her to regenerate as long as one of her 'clones' remains, making her incredibly hard to kill. In her full sura form, Ravana is capable of sustaining the damage caused by Ananta taking on his own sura form.[5] Ravana is regarded as the strongest No.2 outside of the Kings when in full sura form.[6]

Ravana's regeneration is so powerful that he can regenerate from being entirely ripped apart very quickly, needing to be evaporated entirely to gain some time.[7] This makes Ravana pretty careless, as he enjoys to play dead and stab people in the back when they don't expect it.[8]

Appearance
In human form, Hura has a slender and androgynous appearance. He has pale purple skin and long, dark, purplish-grey straight hair which is cut slightly diagonally in front (covering his right eye). Hura has a pink left eye, with a pink pupil, a sharp and slightly elongated nose and unnaturally long and thin fingers. He has four arms, but usually hides two under his cloak. He wears pink high-heel clogs and a purplish-black suit that covers the lower part of his body as well his arms and hands, with stirrups around the feet and shoes. In his sura form, he looks insect-like and is quite small compared to other suras.  His body is purplish-black colored and he has two legs, four arms, and four insect-wings. He has a pink pattern on his legs, scales, and upper parts of the wings.

Personality

He has a mischievous personality and has been shown playing around and daring other suras for fun. Hura seems to get bored quickly and is not suited for waiting, and his impatience causes him to repeat his mistakes and annoy other people. He doesn't care for others' opinions and dislikes following orders. For example, despite being sent to help Sagara's army, he refuses to do as Riagara says because he isn't an Ananta and, as such, shouldn't have to answer to her. Even though he likes to brag about himself, whenever things get dangerous he's quick to back away. Upon realizing that Kasak is the equivalent of a 5th-stage rakshasa, he complains no one warned him about facing someone like him and Riagara manages to make him admit he refused to eliminate the humans in Atera because he was scared, since there were a lot of magicians.

He is equally rude to everyone, regardless of rank. He lacks the sense to watch what he says around those who are stronger than him. He would have been dead ages ago if it were not for his incredible regeneration speed and his ability to resurrect multiple times.[2]

Despite his attitude, he seems to understand more of what is going on than the other suras in Sagara's group, and has his own agenda that may not necessarily line up with theirs. He knows about the power of names and deduces from Maruna and Yuta's conversation during their battle that the power of the Garuda clan's name lies with Yuta.[3] He also interferes with Clophe and Cloche twice: once threatening to eat them to prevent them from reuniting with Sagara when she was about to fight Agni,[1] and another time taking Clophe hostage to coerce Cloche to follow him out of the radius of Asha's hoti vishnu.[4]

Appearance

She has thick long green hair that she keeps untied, but tied in a wide ponytail with a green ribbon in her earlier stages. Shakun has green eyes and green eyebrows and light-green ears that appear as pointy formations of skin or hair. She has two similar formations on her back, that like her ears, grows more dense as she ages. Shakuntala wears a long green sleeveless dress with a neck guard that leaves her back bare. As an adult, she also wears two green sleeves that are fastened to her arms by thin green ribbons. Like her father Gandharva, she is often seen barefoot. Shakuntala is said to resemble Menaka|her mother greatly.

Shakuntala's sura form is like an octopus or a sea anemone. When in her sura form she has green tentacles, which can be seen vaguely seen during the attack on Kalibloom. As at this stage she had been absorbed by a taraka the real appearance of her sura form may be slightly different.

Personality
Shakuntala has a pacifistic and modest personality. Throughout her life, her father has been extremely overprotective of her. She seems to like flowers, and is often seen kneeling on a bed of flowers while composing a chain of flowers.

She was fond of Maruna, insisting to his father they should take him in. They spent a long time together, while the Garuda rakshasa trained with her father. Shakun enjoyed teasing Maruna in an affectionate way, which annoyed him a lot when he was in his 3rd stage and still immature.

She was also fond of children and was often found playing and taking care of them. Whenever she had the chance, she would help the weakest of the Gandharva clan. Shakuntala is very selfless, stating once that to "stay [there], with the other children, until the end" was enough for her.

Skills and Abilities
Not much is known about Shakuntala's abilities, as she never had to use them in a fight as her father protected her from everything. The only abilities she has shown are more recovery based than either defensive or offensive. Despite her royal heritage, Shakuntala is weak for a sura, as shown by her unusually fast development. Her weakness is notable because both of her parents are strong nastikas.[2]

Healing Abilities: She has healing skills, and often uses them on herself because of her low tolerance for the toxic environment of the sura realm.[3]

A young Shakuntala was kidnapped by the gods, but is returned to Gandharva by Agni, who thus saves both Gandharva's and Shakuntala's life. As a result of this, later on she made her father promise her he would not fight Agni.

She is often shown to be arranging flowers, making bouquets and daisy chains. While rarely wearing one herself, she has equipped both Gandharva and Maruna with one. Her modest ways have at one point calmed a maddened Maruna.

Upon realizing how important she was to her father, she requested personally, that if she was used as a bait ever again, he would not go out of his way to save her. She claims that she understands she is important for him, but that Gandharva is more important for the clan.

By the year N0, Shakuntala and the rest of her clan were forced to adapt to the sura realm. She's seen with Urvasi commenting on the danger of the atmosphere for the little ones. History
Garuda is a nastika, and the king of the Garuda clan. Over the billions of years of his existence, he has had many children, but only his three youngest still survive. 

A long time ago, Garuda agreed into undergoing an alliance with Gandharva and Shuri. This alliance developed into a strong friendship, also shared by the primeval god Visnu.[8]

Garuda has three living children. His wife Vinata was the mother of the oldest, Maruna, and the youngest, Kalavinka; his middle child, Yuta, resulted from a mysterious relationship with primeval god Kali.[9] Eventually, he took Yuta in at the Garuda clan stronghold when his son escaped from Taraka about 300 years ago, and continued to raise him there.[6]

However, the three siblings had to go into hiding because of the power of names. Maruna was sent to Gandharva on Planet Carte, Yuta to Shuri on Planet Isholy, and Kalavinka to Vishnu on Planet Willarv.[8]

In the year N0, Garuda's wife Vinata died and Garuda slipped into a coma. When the boundary between realms was closed off by primeval god Vishnu, this resulted in Garuda, in the sura realm, being cut off from his name holder, theorized by Akasha to be either Yuta or Kalavinka, both in the human realm.[10]

Vinata's death put Akasha as the second-strongest in the clan, who forced Maruna to develop into his 4th stage and ordered him to either bring his siblings back to the sura realm alive or kill them, in a bid to awaken Garuda.[6][10]

Samphati

Samphati is a rakshasa from the Garuda clan. She joins Sagara's crew in order to aid in the attack on Rindhallow. She is the first 5th-stage rakshasa to make an appearance in the webtoon.

Appearance
4th Stage
Human Form
When she was in 4th stage, Samphati had the appearance of a teenage girl. Unlike in her 5th stage, both her legs were surafied.[1] She wore a v-neck dress with large open sleeves.

5th Stage
Human Form
Samphati appears as a beautiful young woman with long blonde hair and empty, lime-colored eyes. Her only visible sura trait is her right foot, which is a red claw. She wears a ruffled short black dress, a red sandal on her left foot, red drop-shaped earrings, and two roses with black feathers in her hair. Her Garuda wings are the same color as her hair.[2] At least one sura has said that she could easily be mistaken for a nastika.[3]

Sura Form
In sura form, Samphati appears as an enormous humanoid.[4] She has a pink spindly mask covering her face and spines of the same color jutting out of her back. A small tuft of black feathers cover her chest, but she is naked from the waist down. Her feet are red claws, similar to her right foot in human form, and her shins are covered in pink armor. A spiky, oblong black claw floats beside her, from which she can fire transcendentals.[5]

Tarakified Sura Form
After becoming a Taraka, Samphati's sura form is slightly changed. She remains similar in appearance, tinted red with some texture changes.

Personality
She does not talk much and willingly obeys Akasha. She seems to not care much about others, showing no reaction to the talk of other rakshasas and casually breaking Maruna's arm. She shows no obvious emotions, only slightly scowling when Maruna mentions the name Jatayu. This could be due to her stunted emotional capacity that resulted from her abnormally-fast development to 5th stage.[3] This is something she overcomes only after being Tarakafied, and realizing that Yuta was not the one to blame for her sister's death.

She is, respectful to her superiors, and has even bowed to Sagara in deference to her.[6] A result of her being raised by Akasha, repeating the doctrine and belief that power is everything in this world. She had a softer side during her 4th stage, saving an Upani out of compassion for Maruna.[1]

Skills and Abilities

As a 5th-Stage Rakshasa, Samphati is an incredibly powerful rakshasa. However, It was noted by Maruna (who is a very powerful Rakshasa) that their power difference is very noticeable (when he too is in 5th-Stage).

Garuda Clan Eyesight: She has extremely keen eyesight, to the point that she was able to search for Yuta's location on the surface of the planet from her vantage point in space.[2]

Healing Factor: Like all Rakshasas, Samphati is capable of healing herself after getting hurt.

Teleportation: She has a teleport skill she uses to show up when Akasha calls for her,[3] and when taking her leave from Maruna when she leaves to search for Yuta.[7]

Physical Strength: She also possesses a tremendous amount of physical strength, since she could easily overpower Maruna in his 3rd stage and cause the side of a mountain to collapse with a single step. She is also able to suppress her strength, temporarily fooling Yuta into thinking she could be an upani.[8]

Passive Vigor Recovery: As a 5th-stage rakshasa, she does not require food to recover her vigor, and she is able to beat Maruna for months at a time before her vigor runs out. She also used recovery transcendentals to "repair" Maruna during his "training" so she could continue to beat him without any need to stop for him to regenerate.[9]

Psychological Transcendental: When under the influence of a psychological transcendental, Maruna manages to escape as Samphati is the one who had trained him, and psychological transcendentals were her specialty.[10] As such, she is capable of creating powerful and very realistic illusions, trapping people if she so chooses. In Ep.2-166 she manages to trap Yuta within one.

Cloaking: As she has both sky and darkness attributes, Samphati is able to use the highest level cloaking. Meaning that she can use transcendental skills even while using cloaking, without it wearing off. She does this when, attacking the city while remaining cloaked in space.[11]

Sky Transcendental: Similarly to Maruna, Samphati has a transcendental that changes the color of the sky as she attacks. Unlike Maruna, her skill turns the sky multiple colors (purple, pink, orange, yellow, and green) and causes portals to open and release yellow beams.

Shield (unnamed): Samphati is capable of creating a yellow tinted shield to protect herself and others.[12]

Energy Attack (unnamed): Samphati can use a transcendental that creates spheres of energy around her which she can use to unleash blasts of energy at her target(s).

Appearance
Raltara is extremely tall, more so than her father. This is because her mother was very tall.[1] In her human form she has very warm-dark skin, long bright red hair and a beak-like facial mask covering the upper half of her face, revealing her black eyes with white irises. She wears a long black cloak with red feathery fur at the top and white edges at the bottom. She wears this coat closed just enough to cover her breasts and she has black pants.

In her bird-like sura form, Raltara is mostly black, has a red beak and white eyes. Her wings and the feathers around her face are bright red. Her long tail, however, is white. She has sharp red talons on her hands and feet.

Personality
Raltara has a very serious personality. She is resigned to the cruel ways of the world of suras and loyal to the nastikas. In her first appearance, she is prideful for her powerful heritage[1] but as she loses her position she reveals her dedication to protect her beloved younger siblings.[2]

Despite having no qualms with killing humans if ordered to do so, she does not do more than necessary and can be convinced to back down by strength, something which leaves her with no desire for revenge or to get back at whoever stood in her way.[3]

Skills and Abilities
Raltara is an extremely powerful rakshasa, one who other rakshasas would think twice before challenging. The hereditary attribute she received from her mother is destruction, an extremely powerful attribute that is uncommon among suras, this is because the majority of nastikas who had this attribute died in the early stages of the universe. As the Daughter of Garuda and of his second in command early in the universe, she is very powerful for a Rakshasa.

Garuda Clan Abilities: As one of the Garuda clan, she also possesses extreme speed and keen eyesight.

Regeneration Ability: As a Rakshasa, Raltara has an ability to allows her to heal herself from damage.

Raltara has a wide array of powerful transcendental skills at her disposal, most of which allow her to destroy and blow up things.

Defensive Transcendental: She has a shield-like defensive transcendental which prevents attacks from hitting, although the shield weakens whenever when she is attacking.

Unique Transcendental Skill: She also possesses a unique transcendental which she has used in her sura form. This skill forms a giant sphere that Raltara is able to push on her target. The condition for this transcendental is that it requires a celestial body of a certain brightness (e.g. the moon). Therefore she would often choose a suitable environment to fight based on the how bright the present celestial body is.[1]

Forced Transformation Transcendental: Another of her transcendentals allows her to force other suras to return to human form, although at the cost of returning to human form herself.

Offensive Transcendental: Raltara possess an offensive transcendental that enables her to form orbs of energy that unleash powerful pink destructive beams of energy.

Notes
Since R and L are the same letter in Korean, the correct spelling of Raltara's name is unconfirmed. It may be Rartara, Raltara, Raltala, Rartala, Laltala, Lartara, Laltara, Lartala... among these, Lal Tara means "red star".
Raltara's mother was the nastika that appeared in Episode 3-87 in exposition when Kali spoke of the names she possesses.
Raltara's mother was the original second in command of the Garuda clan. She was Garuda's first love and she had a rare destruction attribute. Unfortunately, she perished early on during the existence of the universe.
Raltara is taller than all characters whose heights Currygom ever revealed in their profile.[4]
Raltara is no longer alive during the current story of the webtoon.
Raltara's words in Episode 3-174 exactly mirror Maruna's from Episode 2-76

Her situation worsened after the death of her mother as she lost the backing of her father. After the primeval gods erased her mother and Kali took possession of her mother's name, Raltara’s presence began to fade to the point that even Gods and Sura were effected by it, making them forget her. The earrings that she has worn since her 3rd stage, Currygom said, are not just ornaments, but have a special ability. Its ability is still unknown. She has worn a collar, an item of Visnu, since her 1st stage. The collar has a function of suppressing the wearer's sura traits. If she takes it off for a long time, she loses control of her own aggressiveness and unwillingly rages and attacks friends as well as foes.

Personality
Kalavinka is infinitely kind and cute in front of Maruna and Yuta, but she shows aggressive side to others. Even though she mistook Ran for a Yaksha clan Nastika, she talked down and picked a fight. She also accuses Visnu of being senile. It's the correct way to open collar with the buckle, but she always rips it off because it is annoying for her. After taking off her collar for a long time, she becomes unable to control her belligerence and rampages. Her aggression without the item is very famous even to Nastikas from other races.

But she is warm-hearted. In order to protect Leez and her village, she was hovering the area all night and did not hesitate to fight other suras in N5. When Vishnu said he will go very far and won't come back, she teared up and grabbed his arm "I will find you". But Visnu smiled and said "Don't" and warned that he will be no longer himself when he returns. He said she must not give her mind to someone who calls himself 'Visnu' after Cataclysm. Also, she took Ran, who was suffering from the pain of 'an eye of Punishment', to Yaksha's Stronghold. After she trusted Ran, she was worried that he might leave her, because he was the one that she could properly talk to. After meeting 5th stage Maruna, she tried to put Ran through a passageway that can transcend time, worrying that Ran would not be able to return to his original time.

She is hiding her real name, just like Maruna and Yuta. They do not know each other's names, either.
She developed to 3rd stage before her brother Maruna, who is very competitive. His frustration upon hearing the news of her development was the key to his own development to 3rd stage.[3]
In the finite, Ravana says she is the one least likely to be chosen for the power of names.
Values
Kalavinka lived in the Garuda Clan for a very short time and spent much more time with Gods and humans. She says her identity as Garuda has long since faded as a result. She showed she tried to protect Leez(the human), even at the risk of killing her clanmates and of being against the future Akasha wants. Considering the majority of suras dislike or belittle humans, she is quite peculiar.

But when Kalavinka mistook Ran for Nastika, she started a fight, talking down, revealing a hostile attitude towards Nastikas. When looking at Nastika's attitude towards Rakshasa, it's natural that Rakshasas hate Nastika. But this one is also peculiar because most Rakshasas can not speak carelessly to Nastika, for various reasons such as a gap in power, hierarchy, age gap, training, or indoctrination.

Age
If Visnu had not took her, she would have been a young Rakshasa above 300 years old at this point. However, with Visnu for a year, she spent a dimension where the flow of time is different. The place is assumed as 'hell'. It is said that 100 years there was equal to only one day in the human realm. Thus, Kalavinka is over 36,000 years old in fact. It explains why she became 4th stage so early, even though she has more power and potential than same stage Maruna, who is top class among Rakshasas.

Fighting Power
Kalavinka is currently at stage 4, and even in human form, she is stronger than Sura form of Maruna(4th stage) and weaker than Raltara. She was superior in physical power and could exert more power for a common transcendental. In the same human form, she was stronger than Samphati(5th stage), although it's not applied between sura forms.

She has a special transcendental, which can teleport to the other side of a planet.[4]

While taking sura form, the part of her body is flaming but this is not a transcendental. She can also make her whole sura body flame, like Vinata, but it's considered very dangerous.

When she was in sura form, she emitted white fire, similar to Agni's white assimilation.

Plot

History

Kinnara is the first king of the Kinnara clan. She had issues with her name not long after the creation of the universe. For unknown reasons, Kinnara became too weak for a king, and her second-in-command Airavata grew stronger. [5] Kinnara blamed her son Shess for this.[6] Out of fear of losing her life if she was seen as a mistake that needed to be corrected by Brahma, she allied herself with the gods to exterminate the ancient human race in exchange for aid with stealing the Airavata name.[7] Since then, she has lived with two names and has had issues holding both.[8]


She had a relationship with Vritra until the dragon clan members lost their emotions due to a deal meant to ensure their survival. Kinnara was deeply hurt after their breakup.

The finite
Kinnara appears in the finite, helping Vritra deliver a speech, since he gets easily lost and distracted. They were lovers, so she spent most of her time with him rather than with her clan. She consoled and supported Vritra for the difficult decision he had been forced to make. While discussing the penalty, the dragon expressed his worries over what would happen to their relationship when he loses his feelings.

As expected, their relationship ends when Vritra loses his feelings. He leaves on his own, leaving Kinnara deeply hurt. She pays a visit to Yaksha, where she tells him in tears about what had happened to the Vritra clan and to her relationship with Vritra. Yaksha makes her remember that as the King of her clan, she cannot afford to let her feelings get the best of her. He advises her to get back to her clan and prepare for an attack, since her clan no longer has any allies. Yaksha promised he'd try to prevent his own clan from attacking her clan, and she thanks him before leaving.  

Season 3
Chapter 47: Words That Never Reached You
(12) Kinnara later appears in a dream-like memory of the early universe from Shess's soul, sometime after the dragon penalty, but just before the massacre of the ancient humans. Gandharva is present in the dream mainly as a spectator, as he was not present during the actual event. When Airavata helps the ancient humans develop a god-like weapon to destroy Gandharva, Kinnara arrives with the gods to stop them and to take her youngest child Shess back from Airavata. Kinnara claims that she became weaker but Airavata became stronger when the latter took Shess away. (13) Using a spear that closely resembles the one owned by God Kubera, Kinnara fatally strikes Airavata and takes away her name. As she dies, Kinnara states that Brahma is correcting the universe's errors: first the dragons, now the Kinnaras, because by law the king can only be the undisputed #1. Shess is so traumatized by watching Airavata die that he develops from 3rd to 4th stage.

Kinnara then announces that the weakest king is no longer, that the alliance with the humans is over, and that she stands with the gods until the current humans are eradicated. When the giant weapon created by the humans appears in the distance, Kinnara yells at Shess, declaring that she is Airavata now, and he must stop crying and follow her. Shess refuses, and Gandharva goes to his side. Kinnara declares that Gandharva is no longer stronger than her since she holds both the names of the king and the one stronger than the king, and begins to power up, holding a flaming whip. Gandharva asks her if she thinks it is possible to hold two names, and states that he knows of someone else in the future who shattered his own name when he did the same. Kinnara tells him that if it was impossible, Brahma would not have given her the spear in the first place. She then blames Shess for her loss of power and demands that he take responsibility. The sky is suddenly filled with blue fire, and Kinnara is not seen again before the dream ends and Shess awakens.

Chatan

Chatan is a 5th-stage rakshasa of the Kinnara clan, in N23 he crossed over to the human realm to aid Sagara's plan for the resurrection of Ananta.

Appearance
5th Stage
Human Form
Chatan is a tall man with long dark pink hair and eyes. On the top of his head, he wears a pink mask that covers the top of his forehead and ends with pointy teeth stretching over his eyes. The mask includes sharp upturned horns. He wears a long dark pink coat, with long sleeves and no ornamentation whatsoever. He has dark loose pants.

Sura Form
When taking sura form, the mask on his head extends to cover his whole face like a helmet.[1] As a 5th stage, his sura form takes a humanoid appearance. Chatan resembles a giant knight, with his entire body being covered by what seems to be an armor.

Personality
Chatan is highly stoic, maintaining an unshakable calm as he quietly and persistently fulfills his duties. He does not waste words, limiting his statements to those with meaningful or informative weight. Yet, in this same matter-of-fact manner, he instinctively acts to protect those he believes he should.[3]

He has stated that he refuses to commit murder,[1] with Kamadu stating that Chatan has the skills to control his strength to prevent killing when needed[4], as seen when facing Ran. He also appears to despise his brother, Shess, only assisting him to appease their mother.[5] His loyalty to Airavata is unwavering—he was willing to risk his life against Vayu solely to uphold her orders.[6]

Skills and Abilities
As a 5th stage rakshasa, Chatan is an extremely powerful rakshasa.[3] However, he is stated by Ran to be weaker than another 5th stage he had faced in the past.[7] According to Kamadu, Chatan specializes in Mental Transcendentals but remains skilled in close combat. He is particularly known to have great physical defense and surafication speed.[4]

Physical Skills
Momentary Partial Sura Form: Chatan is capable of surafying specific limbs that are detached from his body, and he launch them at his opponents. Yuta noted that these attack were particularly fast.[8]

Transcendental Skills
Mental: He possesses powerful mental transcendentals that allow him to easily control most humans.[1]

Teleportation: He also has a skill that allows him to teleport others around.[9] These portals seem to be undetectable even to a 5th zen god.[10] They seem to be connected to the Earth, meaning they can only lead to a place on the same planet according to Vayu

Limb Control: Chatan can use a transcendental that allows him to hide people inside his detached limbs. While in the 'limb', the people inside cannot be perceived by outsiders, but they can see what is happening out of the space.

Plot
History
Chatan is one of the many children of Airavata and a younger brother to Shess. He and Shess do not have a positive relationship and Chatan wishes Shess to die, yet protects him because Shess is favored by their mother.[5] Chatan developed to 5th stage long before Shess, who is stuck in his 4th stage.

Appearance
He has jet black hair, grey skin, and crimson eyes. Vritra wears bright colorful clothes of simple structure. He has an intimidating aura.

In his sura form, he is a black and red dragon, like Taksaka and Utpala.

Personality
Vritra seems to be easily distracted and does not like to be King, even looking for a way to pass the throne to Taksaka without having to die. Vritra was a good King, however, being willing to make sacrifices for the sake of his clan so that they might survive.

Kinnara used to be his lover until he lost his emotions. After that, the couple split up and Vritra left his clan.

After the numbing of his feelings, he became the most emotionless sura. However, because Brahma's spell wasn't perfect, Vritra still likes to fight Taksaka. He even tried to kill Ian Rajof because Taksaka's love for her caused him to refuse to fight him anymore.

Skills and Abilities
Vritra possesses Fathomless Fire as one of his unique transcendentals. Outside the primevals gods, only Agni knows of this transcendental.[1] The God of Fire also possesses Fathomless Fire, albeit a lesser version, after he persistently harassed Vritra into unleash it.

Vritra also has skills related to space that allows him to ignore space and return to his nest instantly, even if he is in a dimension that is separated from reality.[2][3] Vritra implies that he has successfully tried and tested this ability in all dimensions he is aware of (when Ravana asserts that there is a 0th dimension that even he cannot escape from, Vritra deadpans that it is "a funny story"). He can also teleport midfight, which he refers to as "not having a sense of space". This is apparently not a transcendental, and thus not affected by Taraka eyes.[4]

Vritra emerged as the strongest being in the universe after Ananta's death.
Unusually for a sura, he is stronger in female form, being on par with Ananta in terms of power. Despite that, he preferred to stay in male form back when he still had a choice.
Apparently his nest is in a dimension lower than the human realm.
According to Asura, his unique transcendental has special conditions to activate.
To date, Taksaka is unaware that it was Vritra who destroyed Ian's village.
Plot
The Finite
Near the beginning of the Universe, the Vritra clan tried to increase their forces by reproducing, only to see the expectant couples die. Vritra visited the primeval gods, who told him the Breath skill of dragons was too strong and threatened the power balance among the clans, so they were not allowed to have children. Vishnu warned him that if things continued that way, the Vritra clan would be the first to become extinct. Brahma agreed to enhance the characteristics of the dragon race (mostly by blocking love and other feelings) and turn them all male, leaving them able to mate only with human females. Their children would obtain the power of 5th-stage rakshasas after 100 years.

Vritra went back and called a meeting with his clan. He explained the situation and the gods' proposal. Most dragons were heavily against the strict measure and Utpala openly protested. The King tried to use this opportunity to start a fight with Taksaka, but to his disappointment, the other dragon supported his agreement with the primeval gods. Before leaving, he congratulated Tak for being able to get rid of Utpala, since all dragons would take male form and she would have to stop clinging to him.

He had a short conversation with Kinnara, where he admitted it had been a difficult choice to make. They discussed the penalty and Vritra was worried what would happen to the two of them when he lost his feelings.

After Vritra lost his feelings, he left both Kinnara and his clan. Like most dragons, he built a nest and spent most of his time sleeping. According to Tak, Shuri, Airavata, and Urvasi searched for him in order to decide who was the most beautiful among the three. Vritra attacked them and they managed to barely survive due to the fact that he was suffering from insomnia at the time and was tired from lack of sleep.

Later, he learned from a prophecy made by Vishnu that Taksaka would fall in love with Ian Rajof from Utpala's line. Dragons in love go into hiding and avoid fighting as much as possible, but Vritra loved fighting Tak. He searched for the village Utpala was looking after and, pretending to be Taksaka, demanded a human sacrifice. The requirement was that the child had to be named Ian. When Ian's parents hid her and refused to hand her over, Vritra destroyed the village and killed everyone except Ian, who was hiding in the basement of her house.
